posts.content: CVE-2026-93987: path traversal in rclone's serve docker volume plugin (1.56.0-1.75.0) lets a crafted volume name create dirs outside the root. CVSS 3.4. Patch still under review, so limit exposure now. #CVE #infosec #rclone https://www.valtersit.com/cve/CVE-2026-93987/

CVE-2026-93987.description: rclone versions 1.56.0 through 1.75.0 contain a path traversal vulnerability in the `rclone serve docker` volume plugin. newVolume() in cmd/serve/docker/volume.go computes a volume's mountpoint as filepath.Join(drv.root, name) from the attacker-supplied `name` field of a Docker VolumeDriver.Create request without verifying that the result stays within drv.root (default /var/lib/docker-volumes/rclone), and checkMountpoint() then creates that directory with file.MkdirAll before mounting. A volume name containing enough `..` components (e.g. "../../../../../../etc") therefore resolves outside the base directory, allowing anyone able to submit a VolumeDriver.Create request to the plugin socket — normally the Docker daemon, or a workload that can request named volumes in a multi-tenant orchestration setup — to make the privileged rclone plugin process create a directory and mount a remote filesystem specified in the same request at an arbitrary host path, shadowing or disrupting system directories. The advisory notes Volume.restoreState() had the same missing validation when reloading persisted volume state. Fixed in 1.75.1.

posts.content:
The memory limit was supposed to stop the request. It became the exploit

[🖼 xplorertech00.wordpress.com/wp…]

PHP2Shell, as a vulnerability, an impact, a public technical chain, and a patch that is not finished until the worker restarts.

26 October 2026 · Defensive reading of Calif, Wiz, and OpenAI · Not an exploit write-up

PHP has treated memory_limit as a safety rail for two decades. Hit the ceiling, abort the request, move on. For PHP2Shell, that story is backwards.

The fatal is not the recovery. The fatal is the primitive. A safety check fires while the engine has already published request state and has not committed it. Teardown trusts the publish step. On the SAPIs that keep the worker, the next request trusts the leftovers.

That is the whole post. The rest is the vulnerability, what it costs, what the public research actually demonstrated, and what “patched” means in a process that is already running.

The vulnerability

[🖼 xplorertech00.wordpress.com/wp…]

PHP2Shell is two bugs in the PHP engine, not in an application.

CVE-2026-109618CVE-2026-109619ShapeOut-of-memory corruptionStale global stateScoreCVSS v4.0 9.2CVSS v4.0 9.2WhenRequest setup, before the scriptA later request on a worker that survivedFixed21 October 202621 October 2026

Both are reached while PHP is still parsing the request. No login. No bug in WordPress, Drupal, Laravel, or the one-file script you deployed last year. The guest application has not started.

The affected range runs from PHP 5.4 through the unpatched 8.x releases. Web SAPIs are in scope: Apache mod_php, PHP-FPM, php-cgi, FrankenPHP, LiteSpeed. The PHP project and the researchers agree the practical risk is highest on mod_php, because that worker shuts the failed request down and then stays alive.

Two engine rules make it possible.

Publish before commit. Some paths mark a structure as live, then do the allocation that fills it in. If the second step fatals, teardown still believes the first step.

Abort is not rollback. memory_limit is a non-local exit (zend_bailout), not an unwind of every mutation that already happened. Shutdown walks whatever the counters say is live.

This shape is old. In 2004 Stefan Esser showed that a memory-limit fatal could interrupt PHP where interruption was unsafe. A 2020 report, PHP bug #78876, and a 2024 audit both touched the out-of-memory behavior. Exploitation was not proven, so it stayed a cleanup glitch. Calif, in OpenAI’s Patch the Planet work, and Wiz, independently, showed the chain holds under default settings. Frontier models cut the cost of a chain that had sat near the edge of manual research for years. That is a claim about discovery cost. It is not a claim that every host falls over on the first packet.

The impact

[🖼 xplorertech00.wordpress.com/wp…]

Successful use is unauthenticated remote code execution as the PHP worker, or a read of that worker’s memory. Wiz describes the second outcome as Heartbleed-shaped: passwords, tokens, and keys that belong to other requests, because the worker is shared. Its heap is not a per-customer enclave.

Calif reports pre-auth confirmation on the builds they tested:

  • WordPress, Drupal, Joomla, MediaWiki
  • Magento, Laravel, Symfony
  • Roundcube, phpMyAdmin, Nextcloud, WHMCS
  • some arbitrary scripts, not only full applications

Those are their results, on their builds. “Default config, before the script runs” is a claim to check in a lab you own. It is not a census of the internet.

What follows from the architecture, without inventing a victim count:

PHP 8.1 and older have no upstream release. Those hosts stay vulnerable until someone backports or the stack moves.

Patching the CMS does not move the bug. The interpreter fails first.

mod_php and PHP-FPM are not the same risk. A startup fatal that becomes the next request’s state on mod_php is often just a dead worker on FPM. FPM does not remove the post-startup path.

A leaked advisory beat the embargo. Scanning around 17–21 October 2026 shows interest. Interest is not proof that every probe achieved code execution. Reliable chains depend on SAPI, build, and whether session.upload_progress is enabled. That setting is a common default, not a universal one.

The public chain, as a technical write-up
This is a reading of Calif’s published mechanism. It is not a reproduction, and it is not a procedure you should run against anything you do not own.

Calif’s analysis is about request startup.

PHP registers $_POST and $_FILES inside php_request_startup(), before the target file runs. Nested form names become HashTables. An empty RFC1867 upload part (filename=””) still creates the six $_FILES slots, and a deeply nested name makes PHP build that tree for each slot. The body can stay modest while the allocator works hard. That is how a request reaches memory_limit without first dying on post_max_size. Chunked HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2 widens the gap: declared length and parsed bytes are not the same check.

The line that matters is the order inside _zend_hash_str_add_or_update_i:

C

 idx = ht->nNumUsed++;  ht->nNumOfElements++;   p = ht->arData + idx;  p->key = zend_string_init(str, len, persistent); /* may zend_bailout() */

The live count moves first. The key allocation can bail out. Teardown walks nNumUsed and treats the slot as a real bucket. The key was never written. The bucket is whatever bytes were already there.

That sequence is CVE-2026-109618. Increment the count, the bucket becomes visible to teardown, the key allocation fatals, initialization is skipped, teardown trusts the count.

The same ordering is the second bug, in session upload progress.

php_hash_environment() parses the multipart body before zend_activate_modules(). Session upload progress may open a session in that window, while PG(modules_activated) is still 0. If parsing fatals, normal module shutdown can be skipped, the request heap is still freed, and the worker does not necessarily die.

On Apache mod_php, cleanup runs even when startup failed, then the process is reused. A later request can initialize the session against PS(id) and PS(http_session_vars) pointing into the previous request’s freed heap. Request A stores request-owned pointers, fatals, skips session shutdown, frees the heap, and the worker survives. Request B reads the leftovers. That stale global state is CVE-2026-109619.

On PHP-FPM, a startup failure takes FPM_EXIT_SOFTWARE. The half-built table dies with the worker. The second bug still exists there, but it needs a fatal after startup so the process is still around to be wrong.

Calif’s useful generalization is the pattern, not a payload: publish or destroy state, do fallible work, then commit. A non-local fatal during the fallible step skips the commit. A later consumer trusts the false state. They used that pattern to move from the HashTable site to session upload progress. One ordering bug, a family of call sites.

Public repositories showed up within hours of the leak. Many are lab-only: a specific official image, display_errors, mod_php prefork, offsets for that build. An offset is a property of a binary. It is not a property of the CVE. Treat GitHub stars as a measure of attention.

The patch

The upstream fixes shipped on 21 October 2026:

BranchFirst fixed release8.58.5.128.48.4.278.38.3.368.28.2.35

Confirm the strings on php.net before you trust a mirror, a container tag, or this page. PHP 8.1 and below are end of life. A distro backport counts only when that vendor’s advisory names these two CVEs.

A patch here means the engine no longer publishes the bucket, or the session global, before the fallible allocation, and no longer lets a bailout leave that object for teardown or for the next request. It does not mean a WAF rule, a disabled ini setting, or an updated WordPress.

Installing the package updates a file on disk. The worker keeps the mapping it already loaded. Until Apache children or FPM workers are recycled, the host is patched and still running the bug.

Disabling session.upload_progress, or changing memory_limit, changes which paths are easy. It does not restore the rollback. The update plus the restart is the fix.

The only lab this post asks for is the one that checks the patch. It does not attack anything.

Bash

 # The CLI binary is not the web SAPI. Check both.  php -v  php-fpm -v 2>/dev/null || true

One script, requested once, then deleted:

PHP

 <?php  header('Content-Type: text/plain');  echo PHP_VERSION, "\n", PHP_SAPI, "\n";

You want a fixed version and the SAPI you expected: fpm-fcgi, apache2handler, litespeed, or frankenphp. Restart the pool or Apache and request it again. If the version does not change, you restarted the wrong service, or the vhost points at another binary. On Debian and Ubuntu, php -v often prints a distro string that is not upstream 8.3.36. Read the package changelog.

For hunting, look for leads. Reporting around 17–21 October 2026 describes multipart POSTs tied to worker crashes and odd session-upload behavior before the advisory. Fatal memory errors on requests that never reached a route you recognize, then worker recycling, are a lead. They are not proof of compromise.

The fatal is part of the transaction

We teach operators that resource limits fail safe. PHP’s allocator fails closed on the next emalloc. The request machinery around it does not. It publishes a bucket, a session id, a global, and only then does the work that is allowed to abort.

That is the vulnerability: an incomplete transaction in request setup. The impact is code execution or a read of a shared worker, before the application runs, on a runtime that goes back to PHP 5.4. The public chain is that ordering, demonstrated by Calif and Wiz on stacks they named, and not a universal one-click. The patch is a new binary in the worker’s address space, not a new package sitting on disk.

Print PHP_VERSION and PHP_SAPI from the process that faces the internet. Match them to a fixed release. Restart that process. Print them again. Anything short of that is a plan to patch, not a patch.

posts.content:
This week gave me Heartbleed vibes again, a vulnerability that haunted everyone for years. PHP powers 70% to 80% of the internet's websites, including widely popular CMS platforms like WordPress and Drupal. Critical PHP RCE (Remote Code Execution) vulnerabilities, registered under CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 and dubbed "PHP2Shell", were leaked online before the official announcement for security patches took place. In fact, some threat actors attempted to exploit them up to four days before the PHP Foundation officially released patches for PHP versions 5.4 to 8.5.

What will make this situation worse in the coming months and years is the sheer number of legacy systems that cannot be updated. This happens for several reasons: the operating system or dependencies has reached its end of life, the software solution was discontinued and left unmanaged, or the sole person managing a fragile system left the company. Often, because a system still generates high profits, no one has dared to update it in years, leaving it hanging as low-hanging fruit for an easy compromise. Many organisations face a combination of these exact issues and many more.

Furthermore, typical patching cycles require a week or two of piloting to monitor for instabilities or system crashes. Companies are naturally reluctant to skip this testing phase, but the severity of this PHP vulnerability means standard patching cycles must be expedited immediately.

As AI makes waves across every IT and Cyber Security sector, the threat landscape is shifting massively. We are now seeing threat actors use AI to reverse engineer solutions and compromise systems before security patches are even available. Years ago, before AI became a mainstream trend, this level of speed would have been unimaginable. Yet, as with every technological advancement and revolution, here we are.

#php #cybersecurity #patchmanagement #php2shell #wordpress

posts.content:
PHP2Shell: What Is Easy and What Is Hard to Exploit

PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, CVSS 9.2) is a pair of pre-authentication RCE flaws in PHP's request parser, reachable through any PHP endpoint on default configs (session upload progress and file uploads). Crashing a worker is trivial but reliable code execution needs per-build memory offsets. The problem is that one calibrated exploit works on every identical stock image like default docker images.

**If your website or application runs on PHP, update right now to PHP 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27 or 8.5.12 and restart all PHP and web server workers, because a patched server with old workers still running is still vulnerable. If you can't patch immediately, set `session.upload_progress.enabled = Off` as a temporary stopgap (it blocks only one of the two attack paths), restart all workers, and watch your logs for memory errors, crashes and web processes starting shells, since a successful attack can look like a perfectly normal request.**
#cybersecurity #infosec #knowledge #awareness
https://beyondmachines.net/event_details/obstacles-to-weaponizing-php2shell-likely-constrain-immediate-widespread-exploitation-0-3-u-e-l/gD2P6Ple2L

CVE-2026-109618.description: PHP uses longjmp() for out-of-memory (OOM) errors to exit the current context and abort handling of the request. Some contexts may not properly account for this scenario and leave request memory in an uninitialized state before performing an allocation. The subsequent request cleanup procedure may read or branch on this memory. Multiple OOM strategies can consistently trigger this condition and lead to remote code execution (RCE).

posts.content:
The memory limit was supposed to stop the request. It became the exploit

[🖼 xplorertech00.wordpress.com/wp…]

PHP2Shell, as a vulnerability, an impact, a public technical chain, and a patch that is not finished until the worker restarts.

26 October 2026 · Defensive reading of Calif, Wiz, and OpenAI · Not an exploit write-up

PHP has treated memory_limit as a safety rail for two decades. Hit the ceiling, abort the request, move on. For PHP2Shell, that story is backwards.

The fatal is not the recovery. The fatal is the primitive. A safety check fires while the engine has already published request state and has not committed it. Teardown trusts the publish step. On the SAPIs that keep the worker, the next request trusts the leftovers.

That is the whole post. The rest is the vulnerability, what it costs, what the public research actually demonstrated, and what “patched” means in a process that is already running.

The vulnerability

[🖼 xplorertech00.wordpress.com/wp…]

PHP2Shell is two bugs in the PHP engine, not in an application.

CVE-2026-109618CVE-2026-109619ShapeOut-of-memory corruptionStale global stateScoreCVSS v4.0 9.2CVSS v4.0 9.2WhenRequest setup, before the scriptA later request on a worker that survivedFixed21 October 202621 October 2026

Both are reached while PHP is still parsing the request. No login. No bug in WordPress, Drupal, Laravel, or the one-file script you deployed last year. The guest application has not started.

The affected range runs from PHP 5.4 through the unpatched 8.x releases. Web SAPIs are in scope: Apache mod_php, PHP-FPM, php-cgi, FrankenPHP, LiteSpeed. The PHP project and the researchers agree the practical risk is highest on mod_php, because that worker shuts the failed request down and then stays alive.

Two engine rules make it possible.

Publish before commit. Some paths mark a structure as live, then do the allocation that fills it in. If the second step fatals, teardown still believes the first step.

Abort is not rollback. memory_limit is a non-local exit (zend_bailout), not an unwind of every mutation that already happened. Shutdown walks whatever the counters say is live.

This shape is old. In 2004 Stefan Esser showed that a memory-limit fatal could interrupt PHP where interruption was unsafe. A 2020 report, PHP bug #78876, and a 2024 audit both touched the out-of-memory behavior. Exploitation was not proven, so it stayed a cleanup glitch. Calif, in OpenAI’s Patch the Planet work, and Wiz, independently, showed the chain holds under default settings. Frontier models cut the cost of a chain that had sat near the edge of manual research for years. That is a claim about discovery cost. It is not a claim that every host falls over on the first packet.

The impact

[🖼 xplorertech00.wordpress.com/wp…]

Successful use is unauthenticated remote code execution as the PHP worker, or a read of that worker’s memory. Wiz describes the second outcome as Heartbleed-shaped: passwords, tokens, and keys that belong to other requests, because the worker is shared. Its heap is not a per-customer enclave.

Calif reports pre-auth confirmation on the builds they tested:

  • WordPress, Drupal, Joomla, MediaWiki
  • Magento, Laravel, Symfony
  • Roundcube, phpMyAdmin, Nextcloud, WHMCS
  • some arbitrary scripts, not only full applications

Those are their results, on their builds. “Default config, before the script runs” is a claim to check in a lab you own. It is not a census of the internet.

What follows from the architecture, without inventing a victim count:

PHP 8.1 and older have no upstream release. Those hosts stay vulnerable until someone backports or the stack moves.

Patching the CMS does not move the bug. The interpreter fails first.

mod_php and PHP-FPM are not the same risk. A startup fatal that becomes the next request’s state on mod_php is often just a dead worker on FPM. FPM does not remove the post-startup path.

A leaked advisory beat the embargo. Scanning around 17–21 October 2026 shows interest. Interest is not proof that every probe achieved code execution. Reliable chains depend on SAPI, build, and whether session.upload_progress is enabled. That setting is a common default, not a universal one.

The public chain, as a technical write-up
This is a reading of Calif’s published mechanism. It is not a reproduction, and it is not a procedure you should run against anything you do not own.

Calif’s analysis is about request startup.

PHP registers $_POST and $_FILES inside php_request_startup(), before the target file runs. Nested form names become HashTables. An empty RFC1867 upload part (filename=””) still creates the six $_FILES slots, and a deeply nested name makes PHP build that tree for each slot. The body can stay modest while the allocator works hard. That is how a request reaches memory_limit without first dying on post_max_size. Chunked HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2 widens the gap: declared length and parsed bytes are not the same check.

The line that matters is the order inside _zend_hash_str_add_or_update_i:

C

 idx = ht->nNumUsed++;  ht->nNumOfElements++;   p = ht->arData + idx;  p->key = zend_string_init(str, len, persistent); /* may zend_bailout() */

The live count moves first. The key allocation can bail out. Teardown walks nNumUsed and treats the slot as a real bucket. The key was never written. The bucket is whatever bytes were already there.

That sequence is CVE-2026-109618. Increment the count, the bucket becomes visible to teardown, the key allocation fatals, initialization is skipped, teardown trusts the count.

The same ordering is the second bug, in session upload progress.

php_hash_environment() parses the multipart body before zend_activate_modules(). Session upload progress may open a session in that window, while PG(modules_activated) is still 0. If parsing fatals, normal module shutdown can be skipped, the request heap is still freed, and the worker does not necessarily die.

On Apache mod_php, cleanup runs even when startup failed, then the process is reused. A later request can initialize the session against PS(id) and PS(http_session_vars) pointing into the previous request’s freed heap. Request A stores request-owned pointers, fatals, skips session shutdown, frees the heap, and the worker survives. Request B reads the leftovers. That stale global state is CVE-2026-109619.

On PHP-FPM, a startup failure takes FPM_EXIT_SOFTWARE. The half-built table dies with the worker. The second bug still exists there, but it needs a fatal after startup so the process is still around to be wrong.

Calif’s useful generalization is the pattern, not a payload: publish or destroy state, do fallible work, then commit. A non-local fatal during the fallible step skips the commit. A later consumer trusts the false state. They used that pattern to move from the HashTable site to session upload progress. One ordering bug, a family of call sites.

Public repositories showed up within hours of the leak. Many are lab-only: a specific official image, display_errors, mod_php prefork, offsets for that build. An offset is a property of a binary. It is not a property of the CVE. Treat GitHub stars as a measure of attention.

The patch

The upstream fixes shipped on 21 October 2026:

BranchFirst fixed release8.58.5.128.48.4.278.38.3.368.28.2.35

Confirm the strings on php.net before you trust a mirror, a container tag, or this page. PHP 8.1 and below are end of life. A distro backport counts only when that vendor’s advisory names these two CVEs.

A patch here means the engine no longer publishes the bucket, or the session global, before the fallible allocation, and no longer lets a bailout leave that object for teardown or for the next request. It does not mean a WAF rule, a disabled ini setting, or an updated WordPress.

Installing the package updates a file on disk. The worker keeps the mapping it already loaded. Until Apache children or FPM workers are recycled, the host is patched and still running the bug.

Disabling session.upload_progress, or changing memory_limit, changes which paths are easy. It does not restore the rollback. The update plus the restart is the fix.

The only lab this post asks for is the one that checks the patch. It does not attack anything.

Bash

 # The CLI binary is not the web SAPI. Check both.  php -v  php-fpm -v 2>/dev/null || true

One script, requested once, then deleted:

PHP

 <?php  header('Content-Type: text/plain');  echo PHP_VERSION, "\n", PHP_SAPI, "\n";

You want a fixed version and the SAPI you expected: fpm-fcgi, apache2handler, litespeed, or frankenphp. Restart the pool or Apache and request it again. If the version does not change, you restarted the wrong service, or the vhost points at another binary. On Debian and Ubuntu, php -v often prints a distro string that is not upstream 8.3.36. Read the package changelog.

For hunting, look for leads. Reporting around 17–21 October 2026 describes multipart POSTs tied to worker crashes and odd session-upload behavior before the advisory. Fatal memory errors on requests that never reached a route you recognize, then worker recycling, are a lead. They are not proof of compromise.

The fatal is part of the transaction

We teach operators that resource limits fail safe. PHP’s allocator fails closed on the next emalloc. The request machinery around it does not. It publishes a bucket, a session id, a global, and only then does the work that is allowed to abort.

That is the vulnerability: an incomplete transaction in request setup. The impact is code execution or a read of a shared worker, before the application runs, on a runtime that goes back to PHP 5.4. The public chain is that ordering, demonstrated by Calif and Wiz on stacks they named, and not a universal one-click. The patch is a new binary in the worker’s address space, not a new package sitting on disk.

Print PHP_VERSION and PHP_SAPI from the process that faces the internet. Match them to a fixed release. Restart that process. Print them again. Anything short of that is a plan to patch, not a patch.

posts.content:
This week gave me Heartbleed vibes again, a vulnerability that haunted everyone for years. PHP powers 70% to 80% of the internet's websites, including widely popular CMS platforms like WordPress and Drupal. Critical PHP RCE (Remote Code Execution) vulnerabilities, registered under CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 and dubbed "PHP2Shell", were leaked online before the official announcement for security patches took place. In fact, some threat actors attempted to exploit them up to four days before the PHP Foundation officially released patches for PHP versions 5.4 to 8.5.

What will make this situation worse in the coming months and years is the sheer number of legacy systems that cannot be updated. This happens for several reasons: the operating system or dependencies has reached its end of life, the software solution was discontinued and left unmanaged, or the sole person managing a fragile system left the company. Often, because a system still generates high profits, no one has dared to update it in years, leaving it hanging as low-hanging fruit for an easy compromise. Many organisations face a combination of these exact issues and many more.

Furthermore, typical patching cycles require a week or two of piloting to monitor for instabilities or system crashes. Companies are naturally reluctant to skip this testing phase, but the severity of this PHP vulnerability means standard patching cycles must be expedited immediately.

As AI makes waves across every IT and Cyber Security sector, the threat landscape is shifting massively. We are now seeing threat actors use AI to reverse engineer solutions and compromise systems before security patches are even available. Years ago, before AI became a mainstream trend, this level of speed would have been unimaginable. Yet, as with every technological advancement and revolution, here we are.

#php #cybersecurity #patchmanagement #php2shell #wordpress

posts.content:
PHP2Shell: What Is Easy and What Is Hard to Exploit

PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, CVSS 9.2) is a pair of pre-authentication RCE flaws in PHP's request parser, reachable through any PHP endpoint on default configs (session upload progress and file uploads). Crashing a worker is trivial but reliable code execution needs per-build memory offsets. The problem is that one calibrated exploit works on every identical stock image like default docker images.

**If your website or application runs on PHP, update right now to PHP 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27 or 8.5.12 and restart all PHP and web server workers, because a patched server with old workers still running is still vulnerable. If you can't patch immediately, set `session.upload_progress.enabled = Off` as a temporary stopgap (it blocks only one of the two attack paths), restart all workers, and watch your logs for memory errors, crashes and web processes starting shells, since a successful attack can look like a perfectly normal request.**
#cybersecurity #infosec #knowledge #awareness

posts.content:
PHP 漏洞通報是個失誤

原發文者承認，自己曾在 Hacker News 提前提及 PHP 即將修補的兩項可造成遠端程式碼執行（RCE, Remote Code Execution）的弱點，編號為 CVE（Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures，公開資安弱點編號）-2026-109618 與 CVE-2026-109619。他原本只是想提醒同樣自行編譯 PHP 的人儘快留意更新，卻意外干擾協調式弱點揭露（coordinated disclosure，讓修補與公開時程配合的做法），使既定公開時程調整，也增加許多人的應變負擔，因此公開致歉並表示願意承擔責任。

他說，發文當下完全不知道存在保密期限（embargo）；他的消息來源告知沒有保密約定，而對方也是從更上游得到相同說法。這起事件讓他深感不安、睡眠受影響，並認為自己的善意提醒造成了意料之外的連鎖效應。他也表示，日後會更謹慎處理未公開的資安訊息。
https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50193416
#php

CVE-2026-109619.description: PHP has various global state that temporarily points into request memory. In some scenarios, global state may not be correctly reset, or may be repopulated after being reset. The global state may then refer to request memory even after it has been freed. Subsequent requests may read or branch on this stale state before it is fully initialized. Multiple strategies can trigger this condition and produce remote code execution (RCE).

Exploit code and details are public for CVE-2026-23074, a Linux kernel privilege escalation flaw in the teql qdisc dating to 2005. Patch now.

#Linux #LinuxKernel #CVE202623074 #PrivilegeEscalation #kernelCTF #ContainerEscape #PoC #CyberSecurity

https://meterpreter.org/linux-kernel-teql-cve-2026-23074-exploit/?utm_source=mastodon&utm_medium=jetpack_social

CVE-2026-23074.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net/sched: Enforce that teql can only be used as root qdisc

Design intent of teql is that it is only supposed to be used as root qdisc.
We need to check for that constraint.

Although not important, I will describe the scenario that unearthed this
issue for the curious.

GangMin Kim <km.kim1503@gmail.com> managed to concot a scenario as follows:

ROOT qdisc 1:0 (QFQ)
  ├── class 1:1 (weight=15, lmax=16384) netem with delay 6.4s
  └── class 1:2 (weight=1, lmax=1514) teql

GangMin sends a packet which is enqueued to 1:1 (netem).
Any invocation of dequeue by QFQ from this class will not return a packet
until after 6.4s. In the meantime, a second packet is sent and it lands on
1:2. teql's enqueue will return success and this will activate class 1:2.
Main issue is that teql only updates the parent visible qlen (sch->q.qlen)
at dequeue. Since QFQ will only call dequeue if peek succeeds (and teql's
peek always returns NULL), dequeue will never be called and thus the qlen
will remain as 0. With that in mind, when GangMin updates 1:2's lmax value,
the qfq_change_class calls qfq_deact_rm_from_agg. Since the child qdisc's
qlen was not incremented, qfq fails to deactivate the class, but still
frees its pointers from the aggregate. So when the first packet is
rescheduled after 6.4 seconds (netem's delay), a dangling pointer is
accessed causing GangMin's causing a UAF.

Oh man, light a candle for #infosec, #sysop, and #ops, cause if you thought the #php #cve was fun, wait till you hear about CVE-2026-111497, AKA as Node2Shell, HTTP2Shell, and Broccoli2Shell, a high-severity out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the Brotli decoder that can permit remote code execution (#RCE). The bug allows data to overwrite memory buffers when a process decompresses untrusted Brotli streams. It was surfaced by #OpenAI’s red team.

Fixed versions were released this weekend, but systems using system-linked Brotli libraries (e.g., Debian, Alpine) must verify their distribution-specific package updates, as the Node.js binary release does not patch those external dependencies.

While researchers from Imperva demonstrated successful code execution on a specific Node.js 24.22.0 Linux arm64 build, no widespread exploitation in the wild has been reported as of October 25, 2026..

Node2Shell \ HTTP2Shell RCE: CVE-2026-111497

ISC Bind 9 DoS: CVE-2026-19630/96888/97313
Windows SMB Server DoS: CVE-2026-91403
Unbound DNS-over-QUIC Bug: CVE-2026-97206
Oracle Java (JSSE) containing compromised eMudhra certificates: CVE-2026-91403

Patching all these vulnerabilities on endpoints and servers will take a humungous amount of time and effort, as it can't be done overnight and is heavily dependent on the size of your environment. It's good that we are getting security patches for software that had critical vulnerabilities present for years without anyone discovering them, like in the Gitlab case where the RCE vulnerability went undiscovered for 12 years across all their releases.

What will happen over the coming years is that we will get a massive influx of vulnerabilities just like the one seen this week, but over time it will stabilise more as software becomes more secure, and we will start seeing fewer vulnerabilities overall.

#Gitlab #eMudhra #Node2Shell #CyberSecurity #Vulnerabilities

posts.content:
Oh man, light a candle for #infosec, #sysop, and #ops, cause if you thought the #php #cve was fun, wait till you hear about CVE-2026-111497, AKA as Node2Shell, HTTP2Shell, and Broccoli2Shell, a high-severity out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the Brotli decoder that can permit remote code execution (#RCE). The bug allows data to overwrite memory buffers when a process decompresses untrusted Brotli streams. It was surfaced by #OpenAI’s red team.

Fixed versions were released this weekend, but systems using system-linked Brotli libraries (e.g., Debian, Alpine) must verify their distribution-specific package updates, as the Node.js binary release does not patch those external dependencies.

While researchers from Imperva demonstrated successful code execution on a specific Node.js 24.22.0 Linux arm64 build, no widespread exploitation in the wild has been reported as of October 25, 2026..

https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/cve-2026-111497

@jschauma For Debian sid/unstable, there is a patched package in the Bug Tracking System by Salvatore Bonaccorso who is part of the Debian security team; his changes are also in the salsa Git repo).

The bug log seems to indicate that the Debian maintainer doesn't consider there is any hurry for sid. So I downloaded the source package, visually inspected the patch, applied it, verified that the two modified source files were now identical to those from upstream commit b418fa81c48262a86a9 which is referenced at the bottom of the Debian security tracker page for CVE-2026-111497, built the source package and upgraded the relevant binary packages.

To be on the safe side, I also uninstalled libio-compress-brotli-perl which is built from a different source package, although that one is quite possibly not affected by the bug (the package was only recommended by other packages I have installed, not depended on).

posts.content:
Node.js Releases Critical Security Updates to Fix Brotli Remote Code Execution and Network Flaws

Node.js released security updates for 10 vulnerabilities, including a critical remote code execution flaw in the Brotli decoder (CVE-2026-111497) and multiple network validation bypasses. These vulnerabilities reside in the core runtime, requiring administrators to update host systems, rebuild container images, and restart all services.

**If you run Node.js anywhere, update it right away to version 22.23.4, 24.22.1 or 26.12.1, then rebuild any containers or apps that bundle Node.js and restart all Node.js services (your usual dependency scanners won't catch this, so check the runtime versions yourself). If you're still on old versions like 20.x, 23.x or 25.x, they will never be fixed. Move to a supported version ASAP. Until you can patch, block Brotli-compressed (br) traffic at your proxy or firewall as a temporary shield.**
#cybersecurity #infosec #advisory #vulnerability

posts.content:
Node2Shell CVE-2026-111497: Brotli Out-of-Bounds Write

Node2Shell (CVE-2026-111497) is a critical Node.js Brotli decoder vulnerability that risks memory corruption and remote code execution. Learn affected versions and fixes

https://thecybersecguru.com/exploits/node2shell-cve-2026-111497-nodejs-brotli-rce/

Node2Shell vuln affected Python too

CVE-2026-111497("Node2Shell")은 Node.js 자체 결함이 아니라 Google Brotli C 디코더의 범위를 벗어난 쓰기(CWE-787) 취약점으로, PyPI의 Brotli와 brotlicffi도 동일한 벤더드 소스를 사용해 영향을 받는다. 공격자가 조작한 Brotli 스트림을 처리하게 만들 수 있는 Python 서비스에서는 프로세스 크래시·메모리 노출·잠재적 RCE 가능성이 있으므로 Brotli를 1.2.1 이상, brotlicffi를 1.2.1.0 이상으로 즉시 업데이트해야 한다. 기사에 따르면 해당 Python 패키지의 수정 릴리스는 보안 공지 없이 배포됐고 OSV·PYSEC·...

https://opensourcemalware.com/blog/node2shell-affects-python

CVE-2026-111497.description:
A buffer overflow vulnerability in the Brotli decoder (c/dec/decode.c) in Google Brotli versions 1.0.3 through 1.2.0 on all platforms allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to corrupt adjacent decoder state memory, disclose sensitive memory contents, cause a denial of service, or potentially execute arbitrary code using a crafted Brotli-compressed stream.





Users need to update any Brotli libraries or binaries between 1.0.3 through 1.2.0 to the latest available version: 1.0.10 or 1.1.1 or 1.2.1.

CVE-2026-113391.description: A vulnerability has been found in DrayTek Vigor2960 1.5.1.6 Revision 8218. This affects the function uploadlangs of the file /cgi-bin/mainfunction.cgi of the component Upload Endpoint. Such manipulation leads to command injection. The attack can be executed remotely. The exploit has been disclosed to the public and may be used. Upgrading to version 1.5.1.7 is able to mitigate this issue. It is recommended to upgrade the affected component. The vendor explains: "2960 1.5.1.7 has corrected many security issues. And 2960 is EoS with limited support, only major issues would be reviewed(e.g. unauthenticated vuln.)". This vulnerability only affects products that are no longer supported by the maintainer.

#Storybook #CVE2026114125 #CodeInjection #JavaScript #npm #DevSecOps #SupplyChain #CyberSecurity

CVE-2026-114125.description:
**Summary:** A malicious website may be able to cause unauthorized file changes in a developer’s project while an affected Storybook development server is running. Under additional conditions, a changed file could be executed by a local runtime with the developer’s privileges. We are not aware of exploitation in the wild.

## Who is impacted?

You are impacted if you run a Storybook dev server in the affected versions.

You are not impacted if:

- You run a dev server that you never open in a web browser (e.g. headless automation, MCP clients)
- You run or visit a built version of Storybook

Recent versions of Chrome and Firefox may ask for permission before a website can connect to a `localhost` service. This reduces the risk, but does not remove it. Do not grant this permission to websites you don’t trust.

## Recommended actions

### Upgrade Storybook

Storybook has released patched versions of all affected major Storybook versions that fix all the vulnerabilities necessary for the worst-case scenario above to occur. 

Upgrade to a patched version listed below before running `storybook dev` again. If you cannot upgrade immediately, do not run an affected Storybook dev server until you can apply the fix.

- 11.0.0-alpha.6
- 10.6.2
- 9.1.21
- 8.6.19

### Review potentially breaking changes

Due to the exceptional nature of the reported vulnerabilities, the Storybook team has decided to change the default behavior of Storybook, including versions 8 and 9, for several network-related features that are not essential to most Storybook users' workflow. If your team relies on the affected features, we've added feature flags that can disable specific security updates to support your existing workflows.

Please carefully read the introduced flags and the consequences of using them.

#### Iframe embedding over the network is disabled by default

Storybook no longer allows the manager or preview to be embedded as an iframe on a website with a different host name. Built versions of Storybook are unaffected and can be freely embedded.

If you rely on embedding a Storybook dev server through a separate web app, run that separate app on `localhost`. You may also use the `security.insecureRemoteIframeEmbed` feature flag to re-enable iframe embedding from any origin.

#### The preview iframe rejects messages sent by an unknown host

Both the Storybook preview and manager now restrict the origin of iframes and parent windows that they can send messages to and receive messages from using the `postMessage` API.

By default, Storybook in dev mode only accepts communication with its own origin and other `localhost` services. Built Storybooks continue to accept communication from unknown origins.

A Storybook addon or integration could hypothetically rely on `postMessage` to update a live story's args. If you do that, reach out to the Storybook team to explore safer alternatives.

Storybook composition also relies on `postMessage`, so a composed Storybook on a different origin now fails to load unless it has been built. The `security.insecureIframeMessaging` feature flag disables this protection, but we recommend you build composed Storybooks instead.

#### The `highlight` event signature has changed

Storybook’s own accessibility addon uses the `highlight` event to inject highlights into the preview, which a user can click. Clicking the highlight opens a menu with a link to a documentation page.

The API for that event was too permissive and could be used to trigger arbitrary events, including events processed by the user’s dev server. We reworked the API to prevent abuse. Besides the accessibility addon, Chromatic's Visual Tests addon uses this API to link to documentation from highlighted ignored elements. Update the Visual Tests addon to version 5.5.1 or later to keep that link working. Because no other addons use this API as far as we know, we have not added a feature flag to restore the old API.

## Disclosure timeline

On September 30th, the Storybook team received a responsible disclosure showing how a malicious website can embed a Storybook dev server's preview iframe and send events to the dev server on the developer's machine.

They combined this information with findings from an ongoing security audit to come up with a worst-case-scenario exploitation of the disclosed vulnerability, and the ones we independently discovered. They then worked to address all layers necessary for this worst-case scenario to happen. We have not received evidence of exploitation in real Storybook projects. The attack outlined in this advisory relies on correctly exploiting a sequence of many vulnerabilities, some of which were never disclosed to the Storybook team.

### Worst-case attack scenario

An attacker-controlled website can interact with the preview of a running Storybook dev server. With user interaction, it may cause the dev server to make unauthorized changes to story files. If a malicious file is subsequently executed by a local runtime, the attack could lead to arbitrary code execution with the developer’s permissions.

🟠 CVE-2026-99018 - High (7.8)

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

riscv: entry: gate shadow call stack reload on sstatus.SPP, not tp

Under CONFIG_SHADOW_CALL_STACK, handle_exception() reloads the kernel
shadow call stack pointer (gp) only when...

🔗 https://www.thehackerwire.com/vulnerability/CVE-2026-99018/

#CVE #vulnerability #infosec #cybersecurity #security #Tenda #patchstack

CVE-2026-99018.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

riscv: entry: gate shadow call stack reload on sstatus.SPP, not tp

Under CONFIG_SHADOW_CALL_STACK, handle_exception() reloads the kernel
shadow call stack pointer (gp) only when the trap came from userspace.
It made that decision with scs_load_current_if_task_changed, which
compares the trap-time tp (read back from sscratch into s5) against the
current tp:

	beq	\prev, tp, _skip_scs
	scs_load_current
_skip_scs:

tp is a user-writable register.  A user task that sets tp to the
linear-map address of its own task_struct (&current) before trapping
makes the comparison succeed (can achieve by brute force with KASLR
enable under our test), so the kernel skips scs_load_current and
keeps running with the gp that userspace left in place.  Under
CONFIG_SHADOW_CALL_STACK gp is the shadow call stack pointer and
load_global_pointer is a no-op, so the compiler-emitted
"sd ra, -8(gp)" / "ld ra, -8(gp)" in every non-leaf function then write
to, and return through, an attacker-controlled address -- an
unprivileged kernel arbitrary-write and control-flow-hijack primitive.
The poisoned gp is saved to task_struct.scs_sp on return, so the reload
is skipped on every subsequent entry as well.

Decide "came from userspace" from the hardware sstatus.SPP bit (already
in s1 at this point) instead of from tp, mirroring the check that
ret_from_exception already uses a few instructions later.  SPP is
written by hardware on trap entry and cannot be forged from U-mode.
Legitimate behaviour is unchanged: user entries (SPP=0) reload the task
shadow call stack, nested kernel entries (SPP=1) skip it.

CVE-2026-99016.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

riscv: futex: untag the user pointer before the atomic access

access_ok() checks untagged_addr(uaddr), but arch_futex_atomic_op_inuser()
and futex_atomic_cmpxchg_inatomic() hand the raw uaddr to the inline asm
amoswap/amoadd/.../lr.w+sc.w through the "+m" (*uaddr) operand.  When the
tagged address ABI is enabled (CONFIG_RISCV_ISA_SUPM, prctl
PR_SET_TAGGED_ADDR_CTRL with PMLEN != 0), those two addresses differ: a
user pointer whose top PMLEN bits hold a tag passes access_ok() after
untagging, but the atomic is then performed on the still-tagged raw
address.

Supervisor-mode data accesses are not subject to the U-mode pointer
masking (that is governed by menvcfg.PMM, which the kernel does not set),
so hardware does not strip the tag for the kernel's own access.  With
Sv57 and PMLEN=16 the tag bits overlap the canonical-address bits, so a
tagged pointer can name a canonical kernel virtual address (e.g. in the
linear map) whose untagged form is a valid user address.  An unprivileged
process can thus make FUTEX_WAKE_OP perform an atomic read-modify-write on
an arbitrary kernel address, with the matching FUTEX_OP_CMP_* result
serving as a read oracle.

get_user()/put_user()/raw_copy_{to,from}_user() already untag the pointer
after the access_ok() check; do the same in the futex helpers so the
atomic operates on the address that was actually validated.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

During PA sync scan setup, hci_le_set_ext_scan_param_sync() gets the
address used for the PA_LINK lookup from hci...

CVE-2026-99014.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

Bluetooth: hci_sync: Fix command skb lifetime during scan setup

During PA sync scan setup, hci_le_set_ext_scan_param_sync() gets the
address used for the PA_LINK lookup from hci_sent_cmd_data(). The
returned pointer borrows storage from sent_cmd or req_skb, without
holding a reference to either skb.

The scan worker runs on req_workqueue while hci_cmd_work() runs on the
separate device workqueue. After the scan worker loads sent_cmd, the
command worker can free and replace it before hci_sent_cmd_data()
dereferences the skb. The command payload can also be freed between
returning from the helper and comparing the address. The connection
lookup's RCU critical section does not protect the command skb.

KASAN reported:

  BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in hci_sent_cmd_data+0x27c/0x2f0
  Workqueue: hci0 hci_cmd_sync_work
  Call Trace:
   hci_sent_cmd_data+0x27c/0x2f0
   hci_le_set_scan_param_sync+0x43a/0x850
   hci_passive_scan_sync+0xb09/0x1460
   hci_update_passive_scan_sync+0x47c/0x6e0
   hci_le_pa_create_sync+0x200/0xa70
   hci_cmd_sync_work+0x13c/0x290

  Allocated by task 95:
   skb_clone+0x13f/0x340
   hci_cmd_work+0x2a9/0x7e0

  Freed by task 95:
   kmem_cache_free+0xba/0x3a0
   hci_cmd_work+0x29c/0x7e0

Use hdev->lock to serialize the address snapshot with sent_cmd
replacement. Protect req_skb replacement and completion cleanup with
the same lock because the helper falls back to that skb. Copy the
address before releasing the lock and use the copy for the existing
RCU-protected connection lookup. Release the mutex before sending or
waiting for commands, preserving the lookup and completion ordering.

CVE-2026-95664.description:
Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an Expression Language Statement ('Expression Language Injection') vulnerability in Apache Camel AWS2-s3 component.



This issue affects Apache Camel: from 4.8.0 before 4.18.5, from 4.19.0 before 4.22.2.



For the object it uploads, reads or deletes, the camel-aws2-s3 producer takes the key from the CamelAwsS3Key message header and falls back to the keyName option configured on the endpoint only when that header is absent. Since 4.8.0, AWS2S3Utils.determineKey() also passed the resulting value to the Simple language whenever it contained ${ or $simple{, so that a route could use a dynamic key, and the evaluation applied to a value taken from the header as well as to the configured option. The header is not route configuration, however: the aws2-s3 consumer sets CamelAwsS3Key on the exchanges it creates to the key of the object it read, that is, the name of the object in the bucket. In a route that does nothing more than consume from one aws2-s3 endpoint and produce to another, the name of each consumed object therefore reached the producer, and a name containing either marker was evaluated as an expression, although the route author never asked for any evaluation, and configuring keyName on the producer did not prevent it, because the header took precedence. A key that a route copied into the header from other message content was evaluated in the same way. Anyone able to choose the name of an object in a bucket that such a route consumes, typically a principal allowed to upload to that bucket, could therefore have Simple expressions of their choosing evaluated in the Camel process. The Simple language can read JVM system properties, environment variables and configuration properties, which commonly carry credentials, and, where camel-bean is on the classpath, invoke methods on beans in the registry. The evaluated result became the key the producer used, so reading a value back additionally required the ability to see object names in the destination bucket, while a method invocation took effect without it; together with the need to name an object in a consumed bucket, this is why the severity is assessed medium. The bucket name went through the same evaluation, but the consumer only ever places the bucket configured on its own endpoint in a bucket header, never a value derived from a remote object, so the bucket name was not reachable in this way. Releases before 4.8.0 used the key from the header as given and are not affected.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 4.23.0, which fixes the issue. If users are on the 4.22.x releases stream, then they are suggested to upgrade to 4.22.2. If users are on the 4.18.x releases stream, then they are suggested to upgrade to 4.18.5. The 4.8.x to 4.17.x and 4.19.x to 4.21.x release lines reached end of life before this issue was resolved and will not receive a fix, so deployments on them must move to a supported release. After upgrading, a key or bucket name supplied through a message header is used literally, so a route that put an unevaluated Simple expression in the CamelAwsS3Key or CamelAwsS3OverrideBucketName header must evaluate it in the route instead, for example with setHeader and simple(), or configure it as the keyName or bucketName option of the endpoint. For deployments that cannot upgrade immediately, do not let a key derived from an object name or from other untrusted message content reach an aws2-s3 producer unchecked: in routes that pass exchanges from an aws2-s3 consumer to an aws2-s3 producer, either remove the CamelAwsS3Key header before the producer with removeHeader(“CamelAwsS3Key”), so that the keyName configured on the endpoint is used, or reject exchanges whose CamelAwsS3Key header contains ${ or $simple{. Configuring keyName alone is not a workaround, because the header takes precedence over it. As defence in depth, allow only trusted principals to write to buckets that Camel routes consume.

posts.content:
This week has been extremely busy. I have seen 4x RCE vulnerabilities, compromised eMudhra CA certificates that spill into their own CVE for Java with a CVSS of 9.1, and 3x DoS type of vulnerabilities, all in very popular and widely used software that can either crash under specific conditions or give remote code execution capabilities to threat actors. The mentioned vulnerabilities are:

PHP RCE: CVE-2026-109618/109619/115560
Gitlab RCE: CVE-2026-110264
Node2Shell \ HTTP2Shell RCE: CVE-2026-111497
ISC Bind 9 RCE: CVE-2026-94300

ISC Bind 9 DoS: CVE-2026-19630/96888/97313
Windows SMB Server DoS: CVE-2026-91403
Unbound DNS-over-QUIC Bug: CVE-2026-97206
Oracle Java (JSSE) containing compromised eMudhra certificates: CVE-2026-91403

Patching all these vulnerabilities on endpoints and servers will take a humungous amount of time and effort, as it can't be done overnight and is heavily dependent on the size of your environment. It's good that we are getting security patches for software that had critical vulnerabilities present for years without anyone discovering them, like in the Gitlab case where the RCE vulnerability went undiscovered for 12 years across all their releases.

What will happen over the coming years is that we will get a massive influx of vulnerabilities just like the one seen this week, but over time it will stabilise more as software becomes more secure, and we will start seeing fewer vulnerabilities overall.

#Linux #LinuxKernel #CVE202643501 #IPv6 #kernelCTF #ContainerEscape #PoC #CyberSecurity

CVE-2026-43501.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ipv6: rpl: reserve mac_len headroom when recompressed SRH grows

ipv6_rpl_srh_rcv() decompresses an RFC 6554 Source Routing Header, swaps
the next segment into ipv6_hdr->daddr, recompresses, then pulls the old
header and pushes the new one plus the IPv6 header back.  The
recompressed header can be larger than the received one when the swap
reduces the common-prefix length the segments share with daddr (CmprI=0,
CmprE>0, seg[0][0] != daddr[0] gives the maximum +8 bytes).

pskb_expand_head() was gated on segments_left == 0, so on earlier
segments the push consumed unchecked headroom.  Once skb_push() leaves
fewer than skb->mac_len bytes in front of data,
skb_mac_header_rebuild()'s call to:

	skb_set_mac_header(skb, -skb->mac_len);

will store (data - head) - mac_len into the u16 mac_header field, which
wraps to ~65530, and the following memmove() writes mac_len bytes ~64KiB
past skb->head.

A single AF_INET6/SOCK_RAW/IPV6_HDRINCL packet over lo with a two
segment type-3 SRH (CmprI=0, CmprE=15) reaches headroom 8 after one
pass; KASAN reports a 14-byte OOB write in ipv6_rthdr_rcv.

Fix this by expanding the head whenever the remaining room is less than
the push size plus mac_len, and request that much extra so the rebuilt
MAC header fits afterwards.

CVE-2026-99013.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

Bluetooth: ISO: Reject concurrent BIS listener setup

iso_sock_listen() drops the socket lock before calling iso_listen_bis()
to preserve the hdev->lock ordering. Two concurrent listen() calls on
the same broadcast socket can therefore both observe BT_BOUND. Caller
A can attach connA and release the locks, then caller B can acquire
them and attach connB before A publishes BT_LISTEN.

__iso_chan_add() checks whether connB already has a socket, but not
whether the socket already has a connection. The second attachment
overwrites iso_pi(sk)->conn, leaking the connA reference and leaving
connA->sk intact. Socket teardown follows connB, so later events on
connA can cause a stale socket access.

Recheck BT_BOUND and require iso_pi(sk)->conn to be NULL after taking
both the HCI device and socket locks in iso_listen_bis(). The connection
check also covers the interval between attachment and publication of
BT_LISTEN. Reject a competing setup with -EBADFD through the existing
unlock path before allocating another connection.

A recorded KASAN report from an instrumented kernel shows:

  BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in iso_sock_hold+0x119/0x1f0
  Call Trace:
   iso_sock_hold+0x119/0x1f0
   iso_conn_del+0xe4/0x270
   hci_disconn_complete_evt+0x351/0x8c0
   hci_event_packet+0x71b/0xb20
   hci_rx_work+0x293/0x730

  Allocated by task 93:
   sk_prot_alloc+0x113/0x220
   sk_alloc+0x2b/0x6d0
   bt_sock_alloc+0x29/0x370
   iso_sock_alloc.constprop.0+0x19/0x300
   iso_sock_create+0x94/0x100

  Freed by task 93:
   kfree+0x121/0x3c0
   __sk_destruct+0x42b/0x540
   iso_sock_release+0x29d/0x340
   __sock_release+0xa1/0x260
   sock_close+0x10/0x20

CVE-2026-99032.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net/smc: protect clcsock lifetime in smc_getname

smc_getname() dereferences smc->clcsock without holding
clcsock_release_lock. Link-group termination can release the CLC socket
through smc_close_active_abort() while the SMC socket is still open,
for example after shutdown(SHUT_WR).

A getsockname() caller can load smc->clcsock, then the termination worker
can clear the pointer and call sock_release() before the caller accesses
clcsock->ops or invokes getname(). This causes a use-after-free; if the
worker clears the pointer before the load, it causes a NULL dereference.
The syscall's file reference keeps the SMC socket alive but does not
prevent asynchronous release of its CLC socket.

KASAN reported the following with test-only timing instrumentation:

  BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in smc_getname+0x19e/0x1b0
  Read of size 8 at addr ffff888109abb4e0 by task poc/103
  Call Trace:
   smc_getname+0x19e/0x1b0
   do_getsockname+0xe5/0x170
   __sys_getsockname+0x8c/0x100

  Allocated by task 95:
   sock_alloc_inode+0x1e/0x280
   sock_alloc+0x3d/0x240
   __sock_create+0x7e/0x430
   smc_create+0x121/0x240

  Freed by task 0:
   kmem_cache_free+0xcc/0x340
   rcu_core+0x50a/0x1850

  Last potentially related work creation:
   evict+0x446/0x6c0
   smc_clcsock_release+0xa8/0xd0
   smc_close_active_abort+0x26a/0x3a0
   __smc_lgr_terminate.part.0+0x137/0x2e0

Hold clcsock_release_lock across the pointer check and the getname()
callback to serialize with smc_clcsock_release(). Return -EBADF if the
CLC socket has already been released, preserving the existing peer
state check and the callback's return value otherwise.

A client-triggered QUIC path migration can enter stream/connection cleanup while a mesh reply still retains a pointer to the DoQ stream. Okta Patches Command Injection and Authentication Bypass in Access Gateway

Okta released security updates for Access Gateway to fix a command injection flaw (CVE-2026-115547) and an authentication bypass (CVE-2026-115546) that allow attackers to take full control of the appliance. The updates also address two remote code execution vulnerabilities in the PHP runtime used by the gateway.

**If you run Okta Access Gateway, upgrade it to version 2026.10.2 or later to fix the admin takeover flaws, and install version 2026.44.0 to fix the PHP flaws. Make sure the Admin Console can only be reached from trusted internal IP addresses, and check for any unexpected admin logins or configuration changes.**

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net: skbuff: don't leave stale bytes in skb_copy_and_csum_bits()

When skb_copy_and_csum_bits() reaches unreadable frags it returns 0
after copying only the linear part, and the ...

#CVE #vulnerability #infosec #cybersecurity #security #Tenda #patchstack

CVE-2026-99030.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net: skbuff: don't leave stale bytes in skb_copy_and_csum_bits()

When skb_copy_and_csum_bits() reaches unreadable frags it returns 0
after copying only the linear part, and the rest of the caller's buffer
is left as it was.  The callers copy into a buffer that is about to go
out on the wire: an ICMP error quoting the offending packet, or a
driver's TX bounce buffer in skb_copy_and_csum_dev().  Neither buffer
is zeroed beforehand, so whatever was in memory there gets sent.

Zero the part of the buffer we didn't fill.  The checksum usually
won't match the data any more, so the receiver will usually drop the
packet, but either way it no longer carries anything it shouldn't.
Only zero for a positive @len, a negative one from a broken caller must
not turn into a huge memset().

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

io_uring/net: populate CONNECT filter fields for 24-byte sockaddr_in6

io_connect_bpf_populate() fills connect.port and connect.v6_addr for
AF_INET6 only when addr_len >= sizeof(...

🔗 https://www.thehackerwire.com/vulnerability/CVE-2026-99042/

#CVE #vulnerability #infosec #cybersecurity #security #Tenda #patchstack

CVE-2026-99042.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

io_uring/net: populate CONNECT filter fields for 24-byte sockaddr_in6

io_connect_bpf_populate() fills connect.port and connect.v6_addr for
AF_INET6 only when addr_len >= sizeof(struct sockaddr_in6), i.e. 28
bytes.

The IPv6 connect paths accept SIN6_LEN_RFC2133 (24 bytes), which
already holds sin6_port and sin6_addr. io_connect() passes addr_len to
the socket layer unchanged.

At addr_len 24 the filter sees family AF_INET6 with port and address
zero, while the kernel connects to the real destination. A filter that
denies an IPv6 port or address is bypassed. Denying connect.port == P
rejects [::1]:P with -EACCES at addr_len 28 but connects at addr_len 24.

Use SIN6_LEN_RFC2133 as the threshold. sin6_scope_id stays zero when
absent.

The threshold mismatch was found by an AI coding assistant (Claude Code)
comparing this hook against the net/ipv6 length checks on my
instructions; it also drafted the reproducer and this patch. I verified
the bypass and the fix in a VM on 7.3-rc6 and that 7.2 has the same
code.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

tipc: hold a reference to nodes found by link name

tipc_node_find_by_name() returns a node after dropping its RCU read lock
without taking a reference. The LINK_SET, LINK_GET a...

🔗 https://www.thehackerwire.com/vulnerability/CVE-2026-99053/

#CVE #vulnerability #infosec #cybersecurity #security #Tenda #patchstack

CVE-2026-99053.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

tipc: hold a reference to nodes found by link name

tipc_node_find_by_name() returns a node after dropping its RCU read lock
without taking a reference.  The LINK_SET, LINK_GET and LINK_RESET_STATS
handlers then lock and access the node, racing with timer-driven cleanup of
a down peer.  Generic netlink serialization does not exclude the node
timer.

The following interleaving can leave a handler using a freed node:

  CPU 0: find the node under RCU and release the node read lock
  CPU 1: tipc_node_timeout() clears the links and unlinks the down node
  CPU 1: drop the list and timer references, queuing tipc_node_free()
  CPU 0: leave the RCU read-side critical section
  CPU 1: complete the grace period and free the node
  CPU 0: acquire the node lock through the stale pointer

LINK_SET also uses the node's media address after releasing the node lock,
when passing queued packets to tipc_bearer_xmit().

KASAN on v7.3-rc5 reported:

  BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in _raw_read_lock_bh
  Write of size 4 at addr ffff88807e06f008 by task poc/92
  Call Trace:
   _raw_read_lock_bh                 kernel/locking/spinlock.c:287
   tipc_nl_node_set_link             net/tipc/node.c:2475
   genl_family_rcv_msg_doit          net/netlink/genetlink.c:1114
   genl_rcv_msg                      net/netlink/genetlink.c:1209
   netlink_rcv_skb                   net/netlink/af_netlink.c:2575

  Allocated by task 0:
   tipc_node_create                  net/tipc/node.c:539
   tipc_node_check_dest              net/tipc/node.c:1196
   tipc_disc_rcv                     net/tipc/discover.c:252

  Freed by task 92:
   kfree                             mm/slub.c:6801
   rcu_core                          kernel/rcu/tree.c:2919

  Last potentially related work creation:
   __call_rcu_common.constprop.0     kernel/rcu/tree.c:3181
   tipc_node_timeout                 net/tipc/node.c:814

Acquire a reference to the selected node with kref_get_unless_zero() before
leaving RCU, returning NULL if the node has already been released.  Release
that reference on every caller exit after the last node access, including
transmission in LINK_SET.  Keep the existing link lookup order and locking
so concurrent link removal still takes the existing error paths.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

fsverity: RCU-delay the freeing of struct fsverity_info

__fsverity_get_info() calls rhashtable_lookup_fast(), which just uses
rcu_read_lock() and doesn't directly synchronize wi...

🔗 https://www.thehackerwire.com/vulnerability/CVE-2026-99051/

#CVE #vulnerability #infosec #cybersecurity #security #Tenda #patchstack

CVE-2026-99051.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

fsverity: RCU-delay the freeing of struct fsverity_info

__fsverity_get_info() calls rhashtable_lookup_fast(), which just uses
rcu_read_lock() and doesn't directly synchronize with
fsverity_remove_info().

For the same inode this isn't a problem: its fsverity_info is removed
only at inode eviction time or upon failure to enable verity, when the
inode no longer needs its fsverity_info and it will no longer be
accessed via that inode.

However, this is broken and can cause a use-after-free for concurrent
__fsverity_get_info() for *different* inodes.  Those rely on following
fsverity_info::rhash_head in the rhashtable under rcu_read_lock() only.
They also use fsverity_info::inode to do the key comparison.

Fix this by RCU-delaying the freeing of 'struct fsverity_info' after
it's been removed from the rhashtable.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

gpio_mpsse_irq_enable() arms the poll worker before publishing it:
schedule_work() runs before the worker is added to priv-...

🔗 https://www.thehackerwire.com/vulnerability/CVE-2026-99050/

#CVE #vulnerability #infosec #cybersecurity #security #Tenda #patchstack

CVE-2026-99050.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

gpio: mpsse: fix race when arming the IRQ poll worker

gpio_mpsse_irq_enable() arms the poll worker before publishing it:
schedule_work() runs before the worker is added to priv->workers. If
gpio_mpsse_disconnect() walks the list in that window it misses the
worker, and once disconnect returns, the USB core frees mpsse_priv
while the orphaned gpio_mpsse_poll() work keeps accessing it, causing
a use-after-free.

Fix this by publishing and arming the worker in one irq_spin
critical section. Teardown walks the same list under irq_spin, so a
worker found on the list is guaranteed to be armed, and
cancel_work_sync() handles it whether it is queued or running.

A worker armed after the disconnect walk would still be missed, so
also set a new priv->dying flag under irq_spin before the teardown
walk, and check it in the same critical section, freeing it via
kfree_rcu() instead when the device is going away, since kfree()
would be called with the IRQ core's raw spinlock held and may sleep
on PREEMPT_RT. schedule_work() is safe to call with irq_spin held,
and the next probe gets a fresh mpsse_priv, so the flag never needs
to be cleared.

This issue was found by an in-house static analysis tool.

CVE-2026-94374.description:
MISP contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in the processModuleResultsData method of the Event model. When processing module results, the code iterates over EventReport entries supplied in the resolved data and saves each one. Unlike the adjacent attribute and object processing loops, the report loop did not unset the client-supplied 'id' field before calling save(). Because the MISP EventReport model's create() method does not strip the id field, an authenticated user with permission to submit module results could include an 'id' value referencing an existing report belonging to a different event. Upon save(), the ORM would update that existing row rather than insert a new one, allowing the attacker to 

 - read the content of another event's report by reparenting it into their own event
 - overwrite the report's fields with attacker-controlled data
 - change the report's event_id to redirect ownership. 




This constitutes an authorization bypass through a user-controlled key, enabling cross-event data disclosure and integrity compromise. The vulnerability requires an authenticated session with the ability to invoke module result processing on an event.

Version affected: <2.5.47

Two threads begin processing the identical response message, received
twice. The first thread, A, run...

#CVE #vulnerability #infosec #cybersecurity #security #Tenda #patchstack

CVE-2026-99059.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

wireguard: noise: reject response consumption after intermediate initiation

Two threads begin processing the identical response message, received
twice. The first thread, A, runs. While it's running, the second one,
B, gets partway through, and during that slow calculation, or even while
blocking on down_write(), A completes and then also a handshake
initiation that's already been queued up runs in thread C, which itself
takes that same down_write(). The handshake initiation creation
succeeds, and sets the state back to waiting-for-response, and calls
up_write(), at which point thread B resumes, because either its finished
its calculations or was finally allowed to acquire down_write(). Thread
B then copies the state back to the peer, and begins a new session,
using that state, which is the same session as the one made in thread A.

Thread A			Thread B			Thread C

down_read()
 sA = handshake->state
 memcpy(cA, handshake->crypto)
up_read()
if (sA != 1)
 goto fail
slow_crypto(cA)
				down_read()
				 sB = handshake->state
				 memcpy(cB, handshake->crypto)
				up_read()
				if (sB != 1)
				 goto fail
				slow_crypto(cB)
down_write()
 if (sA != handshake->state)
  goto fail
 memcpy(handshake->crypto, cA)
 handshake->state = 2
up_write()
down_write()
 if (handshake->state != 2)
  goto fail
 derive_session(handshake->crypto)
up_write()
								down_write()
								 slow_crypto(handshake->crypto)
								 handshake->state = 1
								up_write()
				down_write()
				 if (sB != handshake->state)
				   goto fail
				 memcpy(handshake->crypto, cB)
				 handshake->state = 2
				up_write()
				down_write()
				 if (handshake->state != 2)
				  goto fail
				 derive_session(handshake->crypto)
				up_write()

This seems basically impossible to hit in a meaningful way in practice,
but ensure that it absolutely cannot happen by comparing the ephemeral
private key that's on the stack with the latest one that the peer's
handshake state has.

The comment above strp_done() claims that if strp is stopped,
strp_recv will no longer be called. T...

#CVE #vulnerability #infosec #cybersecurity #security #Tenda #patchstack

CVE-2026-99056.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

strparser: make sure __strp_recv isn't running before tearing down the parser

The comment above strp_done() claims that if strp is stopped,
strp_recv will no longer be called. That's only true if the caller has
a mechanism (eg locking) to guarantee that strp_recv() calls that
started before strp_stop() have completed by the time we call
strp_done().

This adds a dummy lock_sock/release_sock pair to guarantee that any
in-flight strp_recv() (which runs under either bh_lock_sock or
lock_sock, depending if it's called from ->sk_data_ready or strp_work)
has completed.

Only espintcp can be affected by this race condition, but this patch
makes sure no future user of strp can have the bug.

This could crash on strp->sk ("general mode" of strp), but this mode
has been here for 9 years and has never been used. It'll be gone soon,
no point worrying about it.

Switch the stopped/paused/etc bits to u8's to avoid races between
strp_stop() and strp_pause/unpause().

A reproducer has been published and turns the possible UAF into an
exploit [1].

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

tipc: destroy topsrv workqueues before closing connections

tipc_topsrv_stop() closed subscriber connections while the topology
server's send and receive workqueues were still ru...

🔗 https://www.thehackerwire.com/vulnerability/CVE-2026-99054/

#CVE #vulnerability #infosec #cybersecurity #security #Tenda #patchstack

CVE-2026-99054.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

tipc: destroy topsrv workqueues before closing connections

tipc_topsrv_stop() closed subscriber connections while the topology
server's send and receive workqueues were still running. Socket
callbacks and subscription events could then queue more work, and
in-flight send/recv work could drop the last connection reference
during the conn_idr walk.

That race produced several teardown failures: refcount_t addition on
0 from conn_get() on a connection whose release was blocked on
idr_lock, a subsequent use-after-free in tipc_conn_close(),
queue_work() on an already destroyed workqueue from the listener
data-ready callback, and an RCU stall in tipc_topsrv_exit_net()
while the walk spun under idr_lock.

Clear srv->listener under idr_lock so it acts as a shutdown flag,
skip queue_work() once it is NULL, destroy the workqueues to flush
in-flight work, and only then close the remaining connections.
Refuse tipc_conn_lookup() after that flag is cleared, and drop
idr_lock when the teardown walk finds no connection, so an
in-flight subscription event cannot pin idr_in_use while the
walk holds the lock.

v3 supersedes the narrower in-thread diff Tung Quang Nguyen
posted on 2026-09-23. It keeps his teardown order and adds the
lookup refusal and the empty-idr unlock.

#CVE #vulnerability #infosec #cybersecurity #security #Tenda #patchstack

CVE-2026-99064.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

cipso: adjust cached option offsets when removing CIPSO

cipso_v4_skbuff_delattr() removes the CIPSO bytes but does not adjust
cached offsets for options that follow them.

For example, with a valid 10-byte CIPSO option followed by a seven-byte
RR option, parsing records rr at offset 30.  Removing CIPSO moves RR to
offset 20, while the cached offset remains 30.  Consumers such as
ip_forward_options() and __ip_options_echo() then access the wrong bytes;
the latter may interpret packet data as the option length and copy it into
fixed-size option storage.

Mirror cipso_v4_delopt() and subtract cipso_len from the srr, rr, ts and
router_alert offsets when they follow CIPSO.  cipso_len is the distance
the first memmove() shifts those options.  The later header move and
network-header reset relocate the bytes and their offset base together.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net/mlx5e: Prevent stale XSK buffer release on MPWQE refill retry

With AF_XDP on a striding RQ, mlx5e defers releasing XSK buffers until
an MPWQE is refilled. If XSK allocation ...

🔗 https://www.thehackerwire.com/vulnerability/CVE-2026-99078/

#CVE #vulnerability #infosec #cybersecurity #security #Tenda #patchstack

CVE-2026-99078.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net/mlx5e: Prevent stale XSK buffer release on MPWQE refill retry

With AF_XDP on a striding RQ, mlx5e defers releasing XSK buffers until
an MPWQE is refilled. If XSK allocation then returns -ENOMEM,
actual_wq_head is not advanced and a later NAPI poll retries the same
WQE.

mlx5e_free_rx_mpwqe() leaves each released slot marked as releasable. On
retry it can therefore call xsk_buff_free() again through stale pointers
after the frames have returned to the XSK pool and been reallocated.

Set all skip_release_bitmap bits in the common error path of
mlx5e_xsk_alloc_rx_mpwqe(). This matches mlx5e_alloc_rx_mpwqe(). A
successful allocation already clears the bitmap after replacing every
buffer, so retries become idempotent without changing the success path.

Fault injection forced three consecutive failures for one selected MPWQE.
Both an early allocation failure and a partial 8-of-16-buffer unwind
released the original 16 XSK buffers only once. Each error left a full
bitmap, the following NAPI retry skipped the release, and a later
successful allocation cleared it. A 20-second AF_XDP zero-copy pressure
run exercised 1,575,262 buffer allocation failures without invalid
descriptors, WQE errors, or kernel warnings.

In krb5_authenticate(), out_len is calculated to determine available

CVE-2026-99083.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: fix heap out-of-bounds write in krb5_authenticate()

In krb5_authenticate(), out_len is calculated to determine available
headroom in response_buf for the incoming Kerberos AP-REP token. However,
when SMB2_SESSION_SETUP is processed as a non-first element of a compounded
SMB2 request, the calculation omits work->next_smb2_rsp_hdr_off.

This causes out_len to overstate remaining buffer headroom by
the cumulative size of prior responses in the compound chain. Consequently,
the length check in ksmbd_krb5_authenticate()
(*out_len <= resp->spnego_blob_len) passes erroneously, allowing memcpy()
to write the AP-REP blob past the end of response_buf into adjacent kernel
heap memory.

Fix this by subtracting work->next_smb2_rsp_hdr_off when computing out_len,
ensuring it accurately reflects physical remaining buffer space.

CVE-2026-115933.description:
Postiz signs its session, invitation and password reset tokens with one shared secret and without any marker of what a token is for. A route that refreshes the credentials of a browser-extension channel signed data taken from the request itself and stored the result where the requesting user can read it back. A user could therefore obtain a validly signed token containing any claims they choose, which the application accepts as a session, as an organization invitation with a chosen role, as a password reset or as an enterprise provisioning token.

A second, narrower route that creates team invitations signs extra fields from the request body in the same way.
